body: “I release everything either known or unknown to me that has been blocking me from receiving, feeling, and walking in my strength and authority. I trust and discover strength in my body, mind, self, and spirit. I call on my power and walk in my strength.” - A prayer for release Fig 60. Top view of an altar Venus & Libra [ See 'Creating an Altar A Framework for Astrological Magick' for altar suggestions] Place the Kamea for Venus and your ritual candle(s) for Venus on the placement for Venus. Place The Empress and The Justice tarot cards on your altar, as well as symbols for Venus and Libra and offerings to Venus. Ascendant (East): Aries, Fire: Candle, Oil Lantern Midheaven (South): Capricorn, Earth: Salt, Plants, Minerals or Crystals (in illustration Roses, Rose Quartz) Descendant (West): Libra, Air: Powered or Cone Incense, Feather IC / Lower Heaven (North): Cancer, Water: Cup or Chalice of Spring Water Source / Sol (Center): Fire, Yellow or White Candle Petition – You can petition Venus to attract what you desire: love, relationships, and physical objects. Venus can help with beauty, the arts, and being more social. Venus gifts attraction, love, beauty, and sociability. Begin by taking a spiritual bath. Similar to how we cleanse and consecrate items for use on the altar, you must also purify your own energy. You bathe and prepare yourself in cleansing and energetic waters — setting yourself apart from the mundane 'ordinary' life. This spiritual bath can strengthen your connection to the natural world and the Universal Divine; by combining water's vibrational power and raising that water's energy with words (prayer), incense, oils, plants (herbs), and intentions. A cleansing can increase well-being and uplifts your spirit by washing away stagnation and negativity. It can remove obstacles that block success in achieving your intentions. A bath can be done in a traditional bath or by standing in a shower (and pouring the prepared spiritual bath water over one's head). Once you have finished your bath, it is time to create a sacred space. As with any spiritual/meditative practice or ritual, turn off your phone and create space to not be disturbed. Choose a ritual area in your home that is ideally free of clutter, distractions, and technology. You can use sage, palo santo, or even incense to smudge the air. You can also pour sea salt around the area, sweep it up, and discard it outside your home. Set the mood with incense, music, and the soothing sound of bells. Cleanse your ritual candle before dressing it with herbs and oils. As you light the incense, focus on your intention, pass the candle and a written manifestation of your desire through the smoke. Speak or read your intention out loud. Lastly, place your letter of intention in the bottom (underneath) of the bowl of water and place the candle inside the bowl (if using a pull-out candle in a glass jar). Light your candle and visualize yourself in the moment of your actualized and realized intention. 1. Find a quiet, distraction-free place to set up your altar. 2. Cleanse and consecrate all the items you will place on your altar using a method such as smoke, Florida Water, or a mixture of water and salt. Make sure to use new, cleansed candles. 3. Place consecrated items representing the four elements on your altar: Earth (crystals, herbs, salt in a dish), Water (small cup or bowl of spring water), Air (incense or feather), and Fire (candle). 4. Choose a candle and cleanse and dedicate it to your intention. 5. Set up an altar for the planetary god, goddess, or deity you petition, using the appropriate color cloth and other relevant items. 6. Ensure your altar is in a fire-safe area, not prone to wind disruptions. 7. Take a spiritual bath to cleanse and prepare yourself for the ritual. 8. Perform your spell or ritual by placing your written petition, the planetary sigil, kamea, or symbol representing the deity in the center of the altar, along with the candle and incense. 9. Pray. Ask for want you want, and feel it from the center of your being. 10. When finished, close down the ritual. Never blow out the candle. If you need to extinguish it, either snuff it out or pinch it out with moistened fingers. If you need to pinch the candle flame, say, "this light is out, but the intention carries on." Whenever you relight the candle, remember the feeling of the energy, and restate your intention. 11. Give Thanks. 12. When you have completed your ritual, appropriately dispose of the items. Methods for Grounding After Ritual Grounding is an important aspect of any magical ritual. It allows you to connect with the earth and release excess energy, helping you return to the mundane world. While not every ritual requires grounding, it can be beneficial if you feel overwhelmed with too much energy after a ritual. Here are some ways to ground yourself: ● ● ● ● Touch the ground physically, such as by walking barefoot. Visualize roots growing from your feet into the earth to bring balance. Eat or drink something grounding, like a warm meal, tea, or a snack. Engage in physical activity like going for a walk or run to dissipate excess energy. Troubleshooting Spell and Ritual Difficulties If you are having trouble with a spell or ritual, it could be due to a lack of focus or energy or because something in your life is blocking the spell – this could be due to past life issues, karmic debt, or negative energy. To address these issues, try using white or purple candles and performing a series of uncrossing baths and rituals on Thursdays (for Jupiter) for 3, 5, 7, or 13 days in a row. This may help to clear any obstacles and allow the spell or ritual to work more effectively. Understanding the Timeline of Ritual and Spell Results It's important to note that although a ritual or spell begins working immediately, you may not see results right away. According to the rule of three, results can take three days, three weeks, or three months to manifest. More extensive rituals may take up to a year to complete. Keep in mind that every situation is different, and results may vary. *** Taurus Season: April 19th - May 20th 2nd House, Venus Planetary Ruler Abundance & Stability New Moon – Taurus Full Moon – Scorpio Planet – Venus (ruler of Taurus) Day of the Week – Friday (ruled by Venus) Archetype – Farmer Element – Earth Affirmation – I have self-worth Theme – To ground, connect with nature, build abundance, cultivate skills for career/finance Focus – the teachings of Taurus are embedded in self-worth The arrival of Taurus season marks a call to return to the grounding embrace of Mother Earth. As an Earth sign, Taurus reminds us of the richness and abundance that surrounds us. The deep soil nourishing the roots of plants and trees, and the vast oceans pulsing with life, reminds us of the invaluable resources we possess. Whether they be financial, emotional, or spiritual, the earth teaches us to be resourceful and resilient, to build and create from what we have. Taurus season reminds us of our profound connection to the Earth and the abundance it provides. Taurus invites us to sow the seeds of our desires, nurturing them with the rich soil of the Earth. The trials we've faced have honed our resourcefulness and resilience, and now Taurus beckons us to focus on the material realm of our lives - the wealth we have accumulated, the family and community we have nurtured, and the legacy we have created. This season invites us to tend to all these aspects with devotion and care. As Taurus season unfolds, it reminds us that it is not only about what we've accumulated but also how we choose to cultivate it. Venus, the ruler of Taurus, speaks to the importance of aesthetics, the art of creating a space that not only serves a practical purpose but also exudes beauty. Venus, the ruler of Taurus, whispers to us that even with limited resources, we possess the power to craft beauty and harmony. Let us honor the Earth and all it has to offer to find inspiration to live a balanced and fulfilling life. With Venus, the planet of beauty and aesthetics, ruling Taurus, this lunar cycle encourages us to create spaces that mirror our values and bring us joy. The earth supports us in our growth and as we align with its rhythms and take tangible steps toward our goals, we can trust in the power of the universe to guide us toward abundance and prosperity. Let us honor the earth and all that it offers, and trust in the natural flow of the universe to manifest our deepest desires and greatest aspirations. During Taurus season, the energies of the earthy and practical Taurus and the mysterious and passionate Scorpio come into play. Taurus, the ruler of the second house, will guide us to understand the value of our talents, our self-worth, and our material possessions, whereas Scorpio, the ruler of the eighth house, will delve into deeper aspects of loss, obsession, and the unknown. This unique combination of energies from Taurus and Scorpio may bring forth themes of balance, such as love vs obsession, inner strength vs relying on external resources, and abundance vs debt. It is during this time that we are called to anchor ourselves in stability and abundance, by investing in ourselves and cultivating a sense of groundedness. This season may require us to look within and find our own inner resources, and to be cautious of relying too heavily on external ones. This Taurus season may also help us to find a balance between our material needs and our emotional and spiritual needs, by aligning with the natural flow of the earth. It is during this time that we are called to anchor ourselves in stability and abundance by investing in ourselves and cultivating a sense of groundedness. Taurus season will guide you in exploring questions such as: How can I ground myself and have the patience to cultivate skills further? How can I shed identities that no longer resonate with my spirit? What areas of my life/skill can I invest in myself? In what way do you see yourself creatively moving forward? When was the last time you felt lack? If you made a decision based on the feeling of lack, would you have avoided this decision if you had felt abundance or the option of choice? Taurus season light & shadow Taurus energy, when it is not evolved, can be stubborn and resistant to change, with a tendency to focus excessively on material possessions. Without a connection to Spirit, un-evolved Taurus energy may struggle with self-worth, a scarcity mindset, and a possessive attitude towards people and their possessions. At its highest expression, evolved Taurus energy is loyal, grounded, calm, focused, peaceful, artistic, nurturing, abundant, harmonious, and stable. Taurus is an earth sign, and its energy is associated with stability, security, and practicality. When Taurus is unevolved, these qualities can manifest as a lack of flexibility and a refusal to adapt to change. Taurus is also associated with the material world and a desire for comfort and security. Without a connection to Spirit, Taurus energy can become overly materialistic and focused on accumulating wealth and possessions. However, when Taurus is evolved and in balance, it brings stability and security to our lives and helps us stay focused on our goals. It also helps us tap into our creative side and cultivate a peaceful and harmonious environment. Taurus is a nurturing and supportive energy that helps us create abundance in all areas of our lives. By developing our connection to Spirit, we can use Taurus energy to bring balance and stability to our lives and manifest our dreams and desires. Taurus Light / Strength – loyal, grounded, calm, focused, peaceful, artistic, nurturing, abundant Taurus Shadow / Weakness – materialistic, lack of self-worth, need mindset, possessive, greedy Taurus season, 2nd house and Venus Planetary Ruler Taurus corresponds to the neck and throat. Meditating on the teachings and wisdom of the Hierophant (Taurus) and Empress (Venus). We see the neck/Taurus is the bridge between the head (Hierophant) and the heart (Venus). As Taurus season blossoms, the 2nd house awakens, bringing forth the energies of material possessions and financial stability. The grounded and practical Taurus, the ruler of this astrological house, reminds us to look within and examine our personal values and the wealth we possess. This house, also known as the House of Possessions, delves into the practical matters of money, security, and stability. It shines a light on our attitudes toward our possessions and how we acquire and manage our resources. The 2nd house influences our sense of security and grounding in the material world, guiding us to find balance and harmony in these areas of our lives. Venus, the planet of love, beauty, and abundance, rules the 2nd house. Venus represents your attraction and appreciation for the things in this world, whether emotional, material, mental or spiritual. Venus is associated with abundance and gives us a deeper desire for love, beauty, and the finer things in life. As the ruler of the 2nd house, Venus bestows blessings of abundance and gives you the power to attract what you desire. Manifestation and abundance are powerful gifts of Venus, and she reminds us to honor ourselves and the material possessions that bring us joy. Taurus / The Hierophant The Hierophant is the fifth key of the Major Arcana. At this stage, the Fool learns from the Hierophant that there is more than just the material world; there is a divine ruler. The Hierophant, whose name can be interpreted to mean "he/she who shows [the holy]" from Greek, initiates the Fool into the wisdom of the divine realm, where she/he/they learn(s) of the divine mysteries. As the High Priestess taught the Fool to discover spiritual wisdom from within, the Hierophant teaches the Fool to discover spiritual wisdom from external sources: Spiritual leaders, mentors, ancestors, and community. Planetary Ruler – ♀ Venus Symbolism – The two raised fingers in the Hierophant's illustration refer to the holy marriage with the papal cross at the top of his staff. The three crossbars form a triangle that points upwards, creating the symbol for the element of fire. This imagery represents the ethereal body being purified by kundalini, a process of inner transmutation alluding to the alchemical furnace. Lastly, the red roses and white lily flowers are the colors of the alchemical marriage. The three-point crown represents the Hierophant's three roles as priest, teacher, and spiritual king. The keys to the Kingdom of Heaven lay crossed at his feet, symbolizing the fusion of duality as knowledge of the spiritual realm is integrated into The Fool's 3-D consciousness. Astrology – The Hierophant corresponds to the fixed earth sign, Taurus. Taurus represents structure for gentle refinement, development, grounding, and unfolding. Here the Fool learns of morality and the higher awareness of self. The Hierophant's links to religion, knowledge, and traditions passed down through oral teachings parallel the "fixed" teachings that comprise our social and religious framework. The divine union is further referenced in the glyph for Taurus, the cradle of harmony, which symbolizes that that which was separate — the physical and spiritual realms, the head and the heart, etc. — is now united. Upright Meaning – Marriage, tradition, teaching, mentor, a person with experience who shares knowledge with others, moral rules, a spiritual figure or role model, divine wisdom, conformity, orthodox behavior, cultural rules, and traditions, returning to what is traditional, finding security in one's roots and traditions, return or learning of one's culture, traditions, customs, rituals, and ceremonies. Reversed – Old ways, rigid thinking, oppressed by society or religious beliefs, propaganda, obedience through fear, not trust, the pressure of living up to the expectations of others

heading: Taurus Season and Taurus New Moon: Actions and Intentions
body: s As Taurus season unfolds, and the Taurus new moon rises, it is a time to ground yourself in your physical body. Take a moment to reflect on your values, relationships, resources, and finances, and consider how you can cultivate more abundance and prosperity in your life by utilizing what you already have. Remember that Taurus energy is all about self-worth and self-esteem, so honor yourself by prioritizing self-care and valuing your own worth. This is a time to be mindful of your

heading: needs and to take concrete steps to fulfill them. It is also time to align your actions and intentions
body: with your deepest values and to honor the beauty of the present moment. Allow yourself to be nourished by the richness of the earth, and trust in the natural flow of the universe to manifest your desires. New moons often mean beginnings and planting new seeds. With Taurus, we focus on the tangible. What have we built, created, and accumulated? This could be wealth, family, community, or a legacy. Taurus reminds us that our resources are valuable, and setting intentions around increasing abundance and resources will be valuable this season. Taurus is a slow-moving sign, so you may not see the fruits of your labor immediately. But if you're willing to invest time and resources into developing your talents and skills, you can uncover hidden treasures and build a strong foundation for your future. The area that Taurus highlights in your chart is an anchor that could support you both financially (Taurus) and emotionally (Venus). Trust that you have the ability to transform your inner wealth into external material abundance, and embrace your role as an alchemist of your own life. I acknowledge and appreciate the financial resources that I have, and to use them in a way that aligns with my values and goals. I will strive to create abundance in my financial life, and to be mindful of how I can use my resources to support myself and others. I will also work towards financial stability and security, recognizing that having access to financial resources allows me to live a more fulfilling and empowered life. Create an altar – Taurus season is a good time to create a sacred space for Venus, the planetary ruler of Taurus. To create an altar, you can gather items that have personal meaning or significance to you. You might also collect items that symbolize Venus and Taurus. Set up the altar in a space where you can sit and reflect, and take the time to meditate or journal in this space. Observe – Observe and record any symbolisms or messages that you notice during this full moon. A journal is like a magick portal to your innermost thoughts and dreams. Every page is an invitation to explore, reflect, and express yourself in a meaningful way. Collect items – Grab a pen, paper, candles, incense, herbs, and symbolic objects to represent Venus/Taurus, like The Empress, The Hierophant tarot cards, and the Planetary Kamea for Venus. Cultivate abundance – Consider focusing on fostering abundance in all aspects of your life, including financial prosperity, fulfilling relationships, and personal development. By setting intentions towards abundance, you can work towards creating a rich and fulfilling life. This may involve finding ways to increase your income, building strong and supportive connections with others, and fostering your creativity and growth as an individual. Remember to be grateful for the abundance that you already have, and to share it with others when possible. Acknowledge your resources – Take a moment to reflect on all of the resources that you have available to you, whether they be financial, emotional, or physical. Use the affirmation, "I have," to remind yourself of the abundance that you already possess. This can help you to cultivate gratitude and to feel more empowered and capable of achieving your goals. Connect with nature – Spend time in nature and allow yourself to connect with the earth and the natural world. Take a moment to step outside, feel the soil between your toes. Consider planting a seed or tending to a garden as a way to nurture something and watch it grow. This can be a grounding and nourishing practice and can help you to feel more connected and rooted in the present moment. Nurture your senses – Take care of your body and your senses by indulging in things that bring you pleasure and joy. This might include activities such as cooking a delicious meal, taking a relaxing bath, or listening to your favorite music. By focusing on your senses and finding ways to nourish and pamper yourself, you can cultivate a sense of well-being and contentment. Focus on your values – Taurus is a sign associated with stability and security, so consider setting intentions around aligning your actions with your values. Think about what is most important to you and make a conscious effort to live in accordance with those values. This can help you to feel more grounded and purposeful and can help you to create a sense of meaning and fulfillment in your life. Taurus new moon: Rooted in Resilience, building self-worth, and stability We are starting another lunar cycle to set new intentions and refocus our energy towards the gifts that Taurus brings. Taurus brings us back to the earth and life's receptivity, femininity, and cyclical nature. All we have experienced and faced over the last few months have uncovered our resourcefulness, resiliency, and creativity. Foundation and security are what Taurus is about. During Taurus season and the new moon, we focus on the tangible: what we have built, created, and accumulated. This could be wealth, family, community, or a legacy. Taurus reminds us that our resources are valuable, and when we are reduced to minimal resources, we discover our priorities and true values. As we move into the Taurus New Moon, the forward momentum of Aries gives way to a more grounded, stable, and patient energy. This is a time when our focus turns to protecting our material possessions and seeking financial security. It's not the best time for making radical changes or taking big risks, as people may tend to be more cautious and reserved about their money. During Taurus season and the Taurus new moon, our awareness shifts to systemically lacking support. We are being forced to shoulder the burden of incompetence at the most basic and fundamental levels. Taurus exposes where we are lacking and how to create something out of nothing. From this nothingness, we can create beauty. Venus-ruled Taurus loves aesthetics and thrives on beautifying space, even with very little. Taurus embodies the five senses, and the key to manifesting and attracting abundance is to embody, feel, taste, and smell your intention as you call it, into your present awareness. During this New Moon, we focus on our values and then take tangible steps toward creating a life that aligns with these values. These next two months, in particular, we’ll be focusing on and organizing our finances and relationships. If the pressure and feeling of limitation haven’t hit you yet, it might feel like a ton of bricks during this new moon. Taurus's new moon strips away all that is unreal, immature, and unevolved. In doing so, we are gifted with discovery. Many of us need support now, and it's possible that we may see a sudden change in our circumstances and perhaps government support finally coming through. Or we may be disappointed in the lack of support and have to navigate the rough waters without it. Community support will be tested during this time as the collective can no longer turn away from a lack of resources available to those in need. A collective outcry is long overdue, and we might be seeing one during this Taurus new moon. On a more intimate level, we are being pushed to our limits and asked to create a new identity. Being reborn requires faith, courage, and the vision to see a new life and reality beyond our outdated personal and cultural conditioning. If there was ever an ideal opportunity to redefine and reinvent ourselves, now is it. Taurus wants us to think closely about what and who we love and value and weave those threads into the fabric that is being created after the fallout from this time. So as with any new moon, we can use this Taurus new moon to set intentions and visualize what we want in our life. With Taurus, the focus is on love, relationships, values, resources, and finances. If you are one of the many experiencing a time of lack, focus on what resources you do have, and how you can magnify and best utilize them. Also, take the time to visualize what more you want to bring in and how you’d like to see yourself in a different and more abundant life. While these intentions and techniques can help, remember to tend to the daily physical reality, and keep yourself and your loved ones safe and feel loved and supported. Taurus new moon & Tarotscopes New moons often signal the beginning of a new cycle and the planting of new seeds. Taurus' new moon emphasizes the tangible. Your achievements, your creations, and your accumulations. Examples of this could be wealth, family, community, or a legacy. This season, Taurus reminds you of the value of your resources, and setting intentions to increase abundance and resources will be beneficial. Because Taurus is a slow-moving sign, these areas/talents may not be recognized until you invest resources (time/money) to develop these areas and develop your self-esteem so that you are able to access these buried diamonds. This area in your natal chart highlighted by Taurus can serve as an anchor, a support system for your emotional well-being (Venus) and financial well-being (Taurus). Let the light of your life be transformed with ritual. The new moon is a great time to set intentions and focus on what you wish to bring into your life. By looking at where the new moon is activating in your chart, you can gain insight into which area of your life is ripe for manifestation. Use these horoscopes to guide your new moon goals and intentions. heading: Horoscopes & Tarotscopes for the Taurus new moon
body: Tarotscopes is a practice of combining tarot cards and astrology with writing personalized horoscopes. There are different techniques you can use to write tarotscopes. I favor selecting tarot cards that correspond to the current planetary placements, mapping the cosmos here on earth. I use a variation of a 6-card spread as a framework, and if there is another significant planetary movement, ex: Mercury Rx, I’ll extend the spread accordingly. Begin by creating two piles. First, separate the Major Arcana cards into a separate pile from the Court and Minor Arcana cards from the Golden Eclipse tarot deck or another of your favorite tarot decks. Second, select the tarot cards from the Major Arcana pile corresponding to the current planetary places. For example, during the Taurus new moon, the Sun (Sun) and Moon (High Priestess) are in Taurus (The Hierophant). Then, find the Sun (Sun), High Priestess (Moon), and The Hierophant (Taurus), and place the Sun in position 1, High Priestess in position 2, and The Hierophant in position 3. For positions 4 and 5, find which of your natal houses is being illuminated by the new moon (see below), and select the tarot card that represents the ruling zodiac sign and planet for the house. For example, Aries and Mars rule the 1st house, as Taurus and Venus rule the 2nd house. For the 6th position, select a card from the second pile containing the Court Cards and the Minor Arcana, or place the tarot card corresponding to your sun sign. Use this placement to gain more insight into how to work with this new moon illumination. Tarotscope Key 3. The tarot card that corresponds to the zodiac sign the moon is in Ex: The Hierophant (Taurus) during Taurus new moon 1. The Sun (Sun) 2. The High Priestess (Moon) 5. The tarot card that corresponds to the 6. The tarot card Ex: The Tower (Mars), planetary ruler of Aries or a supporting card from the court or minor arcana pile to represent what you want/need to know more of, ex: a card to represent your love life, career, finances, or general support guidance planetary ruler of the house 4. The tarot card that corresponds to the zodiac ruler of the house that is illuminated Ex: The Emperor (Aries) ruler of the 1st house corresponds to your zodiac sun / rising sign Taurus (April 19th - May 20th) & Taurus Rising, 1st House The Taurus new moon is illuminating your 1st house of Self. This new moon is a reminder to honor yourself and all you are. This new moon in your home sign creates some dynamic tension between home, work, and your identity, or how you view yourself within these areas of your life. Maybe a new version of yourself is being birthed, and a reorganization in your external world is underway. Focus on who you are and how you want to express yourself. The 1st house corresponds to The Emperor (Aries) and The Tower (Mars) in the tarot. The Emperor can represent asserting your individuality apart from external, socially-defined norms. The Tower represents a shock, unheeded warnings, or no longer able to deny the truth or sudden change. The Tower next to the Emperor can represent a sudden change in how you present yourself. The chaos of change will eventually subside, and consistency will set in again. The Taurus new moon is in your 1st house, ruled by Aries, and corresponds to the Emperor in the Major Arcana. Aries represents new beginnings and karmic cycles, while the Emperor asks you to find and assert your individuality apart from external, socially defined norms. This is a time to step firmly into your authority and power, cultivating a healthy self-image and personal responsibility. The Taurus new moon wants you to be your own source of recognition and control; instead of letting others dictate your worth and value. Concentrate on how you picture yourself rather than how others see you; draw upon your own wellspring of internal support. This is the time to clarify what you want to call in, what talents you want to develop, and which direction you want to take in life. If you have experienced setbacks this past year, this is the time to strategize on how to face and solve any challenges. With a New Moon in your sign, it’s time to focus on new beginnings and releasing old unhealthy patterns. This is a time of rebirth and redirection. You’re moving to a new experience and will need the self-confidence to get there. Channel the energy of Taurus and Venus to step into your self-worth and walk confidently. Taurus & Taurus Rising Tarotscopes Create your tarotscopes for this new moon. Create sacred space, clear your mind and position the cards and see what guidance comes forth: The Sun (Sun) and Moon (High Priestess) are in Taurus (The Hierophant), illuminating the 1st House (The Emperor/Aries), with ruling planet Mars (The Tower). For the 6th position, place one card from the minor arcana to give you further insight. 3. The Hierophant (Taurus) 5. The Tower (Mars) 1. The Sun (Sun) 4. The Emperor (Aries/The 1st House) 2. The High Priestess (Moon) 6. {extra card} Aries (March 21st - April 19th) & Aries Rising, 2nd House The Taurus new moon illuminates your 2nd house of disposable income and foundation. There’s been a lot of activity in your sign over the last few weeks, and you are emerging with a new sense of who you are and what direction you want to take. Any behind-the-scenes work you’ve been doing will soon be noticed. This is great if it’s been moving you in a positive direction, but also know that any secrets, addictions, or underhanded behavior will also come to light soon. How much you value yourself is apparent in what you’re manifesting externally. Honoring your values, reworking your finances, and exploring your senses and sensuality is most important to you now. The second house is ruled by Taurus and corresponds to The Hierophant in the Major Arcana. The Hierophant is often seen as embodying structure and consistency— two powerful ingredients in achieving success and financial stability. Think of the Hierophant as your guide or mentor — someone with the experience and knowledge to get you on the path to success. This new moon can signal a time to find a mentor or advisor. Someone to help you save time and effort while staying motivated and learning from their experience. So if you’re looking for help setting up proper financial goals, perhaps it's time to seek a Hierophant-type figure who can provide much-needed direction and assistance. While having a mentor or guide can be helpful, it’s key to remember that the power lies within you to take action on the guidance you receive. The more you commit to yourself in the next six months, the more you’ll see your investments, income, and self-worth grow. Taurus’s planetary ruler is Venus, which corresponds to the Empress in the Major Arcana. The Empress symbolizes everything in life that grows and flourishes, representing the Mother Goddess, the cycle of creation, and fertility. She embodies the transformative energy that imbues the mysterious process from seed to fruition. The Empress reminds to be open to the abundance that surrounds us. She symbolizes the time, mental, physical, and emotional change and sacrifice that is required in the process of manifesting. Keep showing up for yourself and believing in your talents, and your beauty, compassion, and creativity will be seen. Your intention for the Taurus new moon is, “even when my patience is tested, I find strength in envisioning my future goals.” Aries & Aries Rising Tarotscopes Create your tarotscopes for this new moon. Create sacred space, clear your mind and position the cards and see what guidance comes forth: The Sun (Sun) and Moon (High Priestess) are in Taurus (The Hierophant); illuminating the 2nd House (The Hierophant/Taurus - leave blank since used in the 4th position), with the ruling planet Venus (The Empress). For the 6th position, place your Sun sign, Aries (The Emperor), and/or one card from the minor arcana to give you further insight. 3. The Hierophant (Taurus) 5. The Empress (Venus) 1. The Sun (Sun) 4. Blank (Taurus/The 2nd House) 2. The High Priestess (Moon) 6. The Emperor (Aries) and/or {extra card} Pisces (Feb 19th - March 20th) & Pisces Rising, 3rd House The Taurus new moon illuminates your 3rd house of early education, communication, community, siblings, and neighbors. With the new moon in your 3rd house, you may find that your social life is more active, and demanding. You may feel inspired to create more structure in your community; by identifying a need; that, if corrected could bring more flow and harmony within your local community. This new moon may provide you with information and the truth about something you’ve been seeking. The third house is ruled by Gemini (The Lovers) and Mercury (The Magician) as its planetary ruler. The Lovers and The Magician allude to the magick and power of connections. The new moon in the 3rd house invites you to seek and give support in your local community. Connect with friends, family, and neighbors to provide support and receive help in return. Whether it's to take on a new project, open a local business, spark a creative idea, or just find someone to talk to who offers you a sense of belonging. If you're fortunate enough to have your needs met and still have the capacity to give back, then why not share it with your local community? You may find yourself offering to help build strength within your local community. This could be organizing raising funds, legal counsel, organizing a board to oversee or physically provide labor and resources to organize construction for a needed community building (library, hospital, fire station, school, shelter, local shop, etc.). The Magician (Mercury) alludes to a time of creation and flow. He calls forth the reality that you can make what you want to happen by mastering your willpower, asking you to gather your tools and resources (community) for support towards manifesting. With the new moon in the 3rd house, choose to find those who can help keep your energetic momentum growing - creating a harmonious flow of energy. Your Taurus new moon intention is, “my word is my gift, and sharing it brings me fulfillment.” Pisces & Pisces Rising Tarotscopes Create your tarotscopes for this new moon. Create sacred space, clear your mind and position the cards and see what guidance comes forth: The Sun (Sun) and Moon (High Priestess) are in Taurus (The Hierophant), illuminating the 3rd House (Gemini/3rd house), with the ruling planet Mercury (The Magician). For the 6th position, place your Sun sign, Pisces (The Moon), and/or one card from the minor arcana to give you further insight. 3. The Hierophant (Taurus) 5. The Magician (Mercury) 1. The Sun (Sun) 4. The Lovers (Gemini/3rd House) 2. The High Priestess (Moon) 6. The Moon (Pisces) Aquarius (Jan 20th - Feb 18th) & Aquarius Rising, 4th House The Taurus new moon illuminates your 4th house of home and family. Think about what makes you feel secure and safe, without getting stuck in stagnancy. The new moon the 4th house may have you rethink how you want to set roots or take steps to nurture your roots deeper. Take this time to consider how family fits into your future, and what steps you can take toward cultivating a deeper family connection. It’s possible you’re in the process of moving or rethinking your home environment. This change brings you to a location that better supports your work-life balance, making it easier for you to invest time in your career without pulling energy away from cultivating a loving and peaceful home life. You could be seeing some changes to your home and family situation right now, or assessing what provides a sense of comfort and security, emotionally as well as physically. Family might need more from you than usual, and this may trigger old wounds, but also help you heal and break free of old limitations. The 4th house is ruled by Cancer and corresponds to The Chariot in the Major Arcana. The Chariot symbolizes being active, in control, and taking direction of one's life; as well as needing to take control of one's emotions. The Chariot is a powerful reminder that you are in control of your actions, reactions, and momentum. And, for many, your Chariot is an extension of your home; where you transport your Self and things from one life event to another. The Chariot symbolizes the importance of having a safe and secure container to navigate life, successfully. Your Taurus new moon intentions are, “everything I build has the power, integrity, and foundation that can last generations to come.” Aquarius & Aquarius Rising Tarotscopes Create your tarotscopes for this new moon. Create sacred space, clear your mind and position the cards and see what guidance comes forth: The Sun (Sun) and Moon (High Priestess) are in Taurus (The Hierophant), illuminating the 4th House (Cancer/The Chariot), with ruling planet Luna (The High Priestess - leave blank for this card is being used in the 3rd position). For the 6th position, place your Sun sign, Aquarius (The Star), and/or one card from the minor arcana to give you further insight. 3. The Hierophant (Taurus) 5. Blank (Luna/The High Priestess is used in 3rd position) 1. The Sun (Sun) 4. The Chariot (Cancer / 4th House) 2. The High Priestess (Moon) 6. The Star (Aquarius) and {extra card} Capricorn (Dec. 22nd - Jan. 21st) & Capricorn Rising, 5th House The Taurus new moon illuminates your 5th house of fun, passion, and creativity. Love, pleasure, relationships, children's creativity, and self-expression are at the forefront for you. Take this opportunity to promise yourself that you will allow and encourage more passions to flow into your life with this New Moon. Does your desire to receive love and validation lead you to abandon a part of yourself that you would otherwise cherish? Returning to an old hobby or enjoyable pastime may lift your spirits. By doing so, you will be able to reintegrate parts of yourself that you may have abandoned. It’s important for you to stay connected to what you love. The 5th house is ruled by Leo and corresponds to Strength in the Major Arcana. The Strength card reminds you of a sacred power, grounded in inner strength and trust, that comes from emotional mastery. The Strength card of the Golden Eclipse tarot illustrates the Fool sitting poised, channeling the energy of the Universe. The lion is a metaphor for the primal energies of the emotional body, the flames referencing its burning passions. Strength symbolizes being in tune with your inner creative flow when time seems to stand still. It symbolizes the power of channeling Source. When you focus on creating from a place of pure presence, you can tap into a field of awareness that unlocks all the infinite possibilities of creation. Your work will come alive and flow through you—not just by you. Your new moon intention, “my humor, charisma, and optimism magnetize love and new opportunities to connect.” Capricorn & Capricorn Rising Tarotscopes Create your tarotscopes for this new moon. Create sacred space, clear your mind and position the cards and see what guidance comes forth: The Sun (Sun) and Moon (High Priestess) are in Taurus (The Hierophant), illuminating the 5th House (Leo/Strength), with ruling planet Sol (The Sun - leave blank for this card is being used in the 1st position). For the 6th position, place your Sun sign, Capricorn (The Devil), and/or one card from the minor arcana to give you further insight. 3. The Hierophant (Taurus) 5. Leave Blank (Sol / The Sun, already used in the 1st position) 1. The Sun (Sun) 4. The Strength (Leo / 5th House) 2. The High Priestess (Moon) 6. Death (Capricorn) and/or an extra card Sagittarius (Nov 22nd - Dec 21st) & Sagittarius Rising, 6th House The Taurus new moon illuminates your 6th house of health and being of service. You may find that your health, work, and daily routines are changing as new information challenges and evolves stuck patterns. The best thing you can do is be flexible. Anything arising right now it to help you break through disharmony and find your way back to health and service. If you’ve been giving to much, now’s the time to focus on yourself. The sixth house is ruled by Virgo and corresponds to The Hermit and The Magician (Mercury, the planetary ruler of Virgo). The Hermit symbolizes introspection for personal and spiritual growth, taking a step back from a situation/person to gain perspective, and believing that the answers one seeks can be found within. The Hermit can also symbolize seeking out a wise person to help guide you. The Magician (Mercury) symbolizes a time of creation and flow. He calls forth the ability to create change, by first mastering your thoughts and willpower to create an internal change, which will over time create an external change in habits and eventually situations. Virgo and the Hermit observe. The Hermit encourages you to purify your mind - to look closely at yourself, so you can start taking note of the ways in which you give too much of yourself. With patience, contemplation, and observation you can make small changes in your daily routines which can add up to create more stability and structure in your life. Your new moon intentions, “I am fully appreciated for the service and compassion I offer to others.” Sagittarius & Sagittarius Rising Tarotscopes Create your tarotscopes for this new moon. Create sacred space, clear your mind and position the cards and see what guidance comes forth: The Sun (Sun) and Moon (High Priestess) are in Taurus (The Hierophant), illuminating the 6th House, The Hermit (Virgo/6th house), with the ruling planet Mercury (The Magician). For the 6th position, place your Sun sign, Sagittarius (Temperance), and/or one card from the minor arcana to give you further insight. 3. The Hierophant (Taurus) 5. The Magician (Mercury) 1. The Sun (Sun) 4. The Hermit (Virgo/6th house) 2. The High Priestess (Moon) 6. Death (Capricorn) {and/or an extra card} Scorpio (Oct 23rd - Nov 21st) & Scorpio Rising, 7th House of Self The Taurus new moon illuminates your 7th house of relationships. Relationships bring reflection. Fall in love with yourself and the rest will follow. Ask yourself: what am I afraid of when it comes to commitment or abandonment? Face your feelings with courage and honesty and allow yourself to be vulnerable. Don't be afraid to ask for support from the people around you. The Taurus new moon is giving you the opportunity to make necessary changes to help you evolve as a person and as a partner. Taurus corresponds to The Hierophant in the Major Arcana; symbolizing finding security in one's roots, returning to traditions, and learning of one's culture, customs, rituals, and ceremonies. It’s possible you’ll find or deepen your partnerships through share cultured or traditions. It’s possible you’re beginning preparations to celebrate the growth of your family: engagement, marriage, baby shower, and the birth of a newborn. The 7th house is ruled by Libra (Justice) and corresponds to Venus (The Empress). Justice signals a time to find clarity, emotional balance, and fairness in relationships. Combined with The Empress, it is a reminder to have compassion for yourself and be your own mother. Sometimes it's easier to be more compassionate to those in your intimate relationship than yourself. Give yourself the same emotional support you would give another. Don't try to change or suppress your emotions - just allow them to be and allow yourself to feel them. Free up space to let your feelings pass through you without holding on to them or judging yourself for their intensity. If you're feeling stuck, ask yourself where you might be avoiding or denying the truth in your emotions. Then, take some time to look inside and get to the root of these issues. You can do this with the support of your friends and family and with a bit of self-compassion. Scorpio & Scorpio Rising Tarotscopes Create your tarotscopes for this new moon. Create sacred space, clear your mind and position the cards and see what guidance comes forth: The Sun (Sun) and Moon (High Priestess) are in Taurus (The Hierophant), illuminating the 7th House (Libra/Justice), with ruling planet Venus (The Empress). For the 6th position, since the Death card representing your Sun sign is already in use in the 2nd position, select one card from the minor arcana to give you further insight. 3. The Hierophant (Taurus) 5. The Empress (Venus) 1. The Sun (Sun) 4. Justice (Libra/7th house) 2. The High Priestess (Moon) 6. Blank {or extra card} Libra (Sept 23rd - Oct 22nd) & Libra Rising, 8th House The Taurus new moon illuminates your 8th house of transformation, Symbolism, Shared Resources, and Other People's Money. It’s a time of transformation and trusting in the unfolding of life. Areas of Intimacy and shared resources are your focus as you learn to trust in yourself most of all. What you thought gave you security, may not be so anymore as you learn to access your deeper inner resources to pull you through challenges. Your natural flexibility will help you ride the waves. You are much more expansive and empowered than you realize, and being in connection with another may remind you of this whether it’s birthed out of a deep connection, or a lesson of disempowerment. Power dynamics that haven’t been addressed are now arising asking for changes in your relationships. Be open to new solutions to old patterns, however uncomfortable or painful the solutions may seem. The 8th house is ruled by Scorpio (Death), with the planetary rulers' Mars (The Tower) and Pluto (Judgement). Judgement represents spiritual awakening, spiritual lessons learned, and acceptance of responsibility. Judgement (Pluto) represents symbolizes the spirit being transformed in the grail of life. This energy can manifest as a sudden desire for a necessary change in lifestyle; perhaps you realize your current lifestyle is not sustainable; or blocks you from reaching your personal life goals. The new moon in your 8th house can signal a time to delve deep into the mysteries of life and explore all the hidden corners of your soul. Now is the time to follow that path if you feel called to shamanism, astrology, tarot, or psychology. You may even decide to become a healer or a teacher. Libra & Libra Rising Tarotscopes Create your tarotscopes for this new moon. Create sacred space, clear your mind and position the cards and see what guidance comes forth: The Sun (Sun) and Moon (High Priestess) are in Taurus (The Hierophant), illuminating the 8th House (Scorpio/Death - blank, since Death is in the 2nd position), with ruling planet Pluto (Judgement/Modern), or Mars (Tower/Ancient). For the 6th position, place your Sun sign, Libra (Justice), or one card from the minor arcana to give you further insight. 3. The Hierophant (Taurus) 5. Judgement (Pluto/Modern), Tower (Mars/Ancient) 1. The Sun (Sun) 4. Blank 2. The High Priestess (Moon) 6. Justice (Libra) {or extra card} Virgo (Aug 23rd - Sept 22nd) & Virgo Rising, 9th House The Taurus new moon illuminates your 9th house of the higher self. Use this New Moon to broaden your horizons both internally and externally to help you see life in a new and fresh way. Other cultures, and traveling helps give you perspective in situations in your life that may feel clogged and stifled. Keep your mind open to new perspectives and new worlds begin to open up. Seeing things in the bigger picture isn’t always your strong point, but now you can begin to see the forest for the trees as new information and understandings help you gain perspective. Learn new cultures, explore new ideas, and adopt new ways of thinking to expand your mind. Which new opportunities and paths did you open up to, and what did these new experiences teach you? The 9th house is ruled by Sagittarius and corresponds to Temperance in the Major Arcana. Temperance guides you to find the balance between the Mundane & Spiritual Worlds. If you live too anchored in the mundane, invite in more of life's mysteries. If you find yourself deep into Spiritual studies, ground yourself in earthly matters. If you can successfully find that perfect balance between your spiritual pursuits and your life on the ground, you can use the wisdom to unlock the mysteries to live an enchanted life. Your intention for this New Moon is, “How can I reconnect to my sense of purpose and spirituality so I can plan my path?” Virgo & Virgo Rising Tarotscopes Create your tarotscopes for this new moon. Create sacred space, clear your mind and position the cards and see what guidance comes forth: The Sun (Sun) and Moon (High Priestess) are in Taurus (The Hierophant), illuminating the 9th House (Sagittarius/Temperance), with ruling planet Jupiter (The Wheel of Fortune). For the 6th position, place your Sun sign, Virgo (The Hermit), or one card from the minor arcana to give you further insight. 3. The Hierophant (Taurus) 5. The Wheel of Fortune (Jupiter) 1. The Sun (Sun) 4. Temperance (Sagittarius/9th house) 2. The High Priestess (Moon) 6. The Hermit (Virgo) {or extra card} Leo (July 23rd - Aug 22nd) & Leo Rising, 10th House The Taurus new moon illuminates your 10th house of career and purpose. Career is your main focus now. You’re discovering more and more about yourself daily and wondering if all the different parts of yourself are being honored and acknowledged in your career. Sudden changes in status, responsibility or direction will further your growth, even if it’s unclear how at the moment. Take a step back from this current timeline and focus on the long-range details. Make sure that whatever you put your energy into, it aligns with your values and is building toward your future. Capricorn rules the 10th house, which corresponds to the Devil in the Major Arcana. The Devil/Capricorn speaks to any false belief that you are trapped or stuck in your current circumstances. Usually, Devils symbolize struggle with a moral problem - lust or love, so it's important to identify and steer clear of any romantic obsessions or fantasies at work which could sabotage your financial freedom. The Devil/Capricorn reminds you that you have agency in your life and that no matter our current circumstances, we always have the power to create change. The Devil/Capricorn also signifies feelings of being overwhelmed with an overthinking or an international struggle. You may realize a shift in your values and beliefs or realize that you have taken on the views of others that are misleading you of your fulfillment. This is a time to set the intention to align your career with your core values and interests. If you've ever struggled with ambition, life direction, status, public identity, life mission, authority, or responsibility, then this Aries new moon is a time to renew and rebirth who you are. It's time for a personal quest that will lead you to discover what matters most to you and how you can use your strengths to help others. It's time to stop waiting for someone else to permit you and start taking ownership of your life. Take time each day to unpack how you want to show up. What story do you want? What experience do you want? Redefine your core values and ensure everything that comes after aligns with those values. Aspire to grow in genuine and meaningful ways, so your ambition isn't just a means to an end but part of a larger purpose. Leo & Leo Rising Tarotscopes Create your tarotscopes for this new moon. Create sacred space, clear your mind and position the cards and see what guidance comes forth: The Sun (Sun) and Moon (High Priestess) are in Taurus (The Hierophant), illuminating the 10th House (Capricorn/The Devil), with the ruling planet Saturn (The World). For the 6th position, place your Sun sign, Leo (Strength), or one card from the minor arcana to give you further insight. 3. The Hierophant (Taurus) 5. The World (Saturn) 1. The Sun (Sun) 4. The Devil (Capricorn/10th house) 2. The High Priestess (Moon) 6. The Emperor (Aries) {or extra card} Cancer (June 21 – July 22nd) & Cancer Rising, 11th House The Taurus new moon illuminates your 11th house of friendship. Good friends are good for your health, and this new moon illuminates the importance of those you surround yourself with. Surround yourself with friends and people who share your same values and vision for the future. Stay close to those you trust. Community and networking are a big focus for you now. Friendships may be changing, and you might find yourself working with groups that are new and different for you. This is good to help you explore new sides of yourself and get exposed to new ideas and visions. The 11th house is ruled by Aquarius (The Star) with planetary rulers Saturn (The World) and Uranus (The Fool). The Star symbolizes one's wish granted, as it rules over the Law of Attraction. Whatever you put your intention towards, you can bring into your reality. If you are looking to be discovered and seen for your art and talents - now is the time to take action and set those intentions. This starts with being intentional with your thoughts, feelings, and who you surround yourself with. If you are an artist: writer, musician, artist, actor, etc., this is a time to set the intention to have yourself, and your work is seen. If you have an established network, use it. If you are starting to build your network and community - put energy into being seen, and discovered for your art and talents. Cancer & Cancer Rising Tarotscopes Create your tarotscopes for this new moon. Create sacred space, clear your mind and position the cards and see what guidance comes forth: The Sun (Sun) and Moon (High Priestess) are in Taurus (The Hierophant), illuminating the 11th House (Aquarius/The Star), with the ruling planet Saturn (Judgement). For the 6th position, place your Sun sign, Cancer (The Chariot), or one card from the minor arcana to give you further insight. 3. The Hierophant (Taurus) 5. Judgment (Saturn) 1. The Sun (Sun) 4. The Star (Aquarius/11th house) 2. The High Priestess (Moon) 6. The Chariot (Cancer) {or extra card} Gemini (May 20th - June 20th) & Gemini Rising, 12th House The Taurus new moon illuminates your 12th house of karma, subconscious, and endings. This New Moon is in your 12th house, the Pisces house. If you feel like you’re underwater, there may be a habitual pattern that’s creating resistance within you, avoiding slowing down and getting the rest you need. Use this time to connect to your spiritual and artistic side. Let yourself dream, meditate, and be inspired by all that’s coming through to you right now. Reflect on your purpose and hold it in your heart, regardless of how much suffering seems to surround you. Everything will pass and everything is temporary. Taurus corresponds to The Hierophant, in the tarot. The Hierophant symbolizes finding security in one's roots, returning to traditions, and learning one's culture, customs, rituals and ceremonies, and rites of passage. The 12th house is ruled by Pisces, which symbolizes endings. You may be in the process of rebuilding one of the structures in your life: such as finding yourself after the ending of a significant relationship/marriage, morning the loss of a loved one, transitioning and rebuilding your life after a significant change in your career (bankruptcy, selling a business, retirement, layoff or other change in your career). You could also be feeling a sense of relief after expending energy into an area of your life; and once the shock abates now that you release what couldn’t be fixed. Learning to let go can be hard; especially since the brain can experience cognitive tension if a task is left unfinished. Sometimes we exhaust ourselves trying to fix, heal or complete something that's beyond our control or simply doesn't need to be fixed. The new moon in Taurus guides you in understanding that you did the best you could do; with what you had. And, when it comes down to what was out of your control, it’s ok to let go and move on. It’s a process, but allowing yourself to not be consumed by the what-ifs, frees up energy for the next cycle to begin. The 12th house is ruled by Pisces (The Moon), with the ancient ruler of Jupiter corresponding to the Wheel of Fortune in the tarot. The Wheel of Fortune symbolizes the ever-changing cycles of life and the endings that come with them. When you can tap into The Wheel of Fortune and remain in alignment with Universal energy but resist it, you can experience turbulent waters. The new moon in the 12 house teaches you that life is all about flow, and when you center yourself within this infinite energy you can trust that it will guide you. No time is wasted, even if you feel like you may have lost months/years on something that recently ended or ended. Remember, when you are in flow with the Universe, you are constantly guided towards a life built on truth, your greater and true happiness. Gemini & Gemini Rising Tarotscopes Create your tarotscopes for this new moon. Create sacred space, clear your mind and position the cards and see what guidance comes forth: The Sun (Sun) and Moon (High Priestess) are in Taurus (The Hierophant), illuminating the 12th House (Pisces/The Moon tarot card), with ruling planets Jupiter/Ancient (The Wheel of Fortune), Neptune/Modern (The Hanged Man). For the 6th position, place your Sun sign, Gemini (The Lovers), or one card from the minor arcana to give you further insight. 3. The Hierophant (Taurus) 5. Wheel of Fortune (Jupiter) / The Hanged Man (Neptune) 1. The Sun (Sun) 4. The Moon (Pisces) 2. The High Priestess (Moon) 6. The Lovers (Gemini) and/or extra card 641 Taurus New Moon Ritual Timing The power of manifestation, to give something form. A new cycle. The energy of new possibilities. Time to set your intentions for what you want to bring into your life. Each new moon is a new beginning. With each new beginning, we are asked to release unfinished business, draining distractions from the past - these are required to be neutralized or integrated into the new cycle for a healthy culmination and manifestation. New Moons often mean beginnings and planting new seeds. Write down your desire to manifest over the next six (6) to eighteen (18) months. Taurus's themes include connecting with the earth, finding beauty in nature, building a foundation, attracting abundance, and financial success. To align your intentions with the new moon, select a time after the new moon alignment. Not before. Your desire is to have the moon ‘waxing’ / growing as you speak, write, and set your intentions. The most powerful manifesting period is the eight ( 8 ) hour window* that follows the exact new moon alignment. * if you cannot perform your ritual within the first 8 hours. You still have 60 hours after the exact New Moon alignment for manifesting

heading: Taurus Season And New Moon Ritual
body: “A strong foundation is what I need to build the abundance and cash flow to succeed.” Fig 57. Top view of an altar Venus & Taurus [ See 'Creating an Altar A Framework for Astrological Magick' for altar suggestions] Place the Kamea for Venus and your ritual candle(s) for Venus on the placement for Venus. Place The Empress and The Hierophant tarot cards on your altar, as well as symbols for Venus and The Hierophant and offerings to Venus. Ascendant (East): Aries, Fire: Candle, Oil Lantern Midheaven (South): Capricorn, Earth: Salt, Plants, Minerals or Crystals (in illustration Bay leaves, Malachite) Descendant (West): Libra, Air: Powered or Cone Incense, Feather IC / Lower Heaven (North): Cancer, Water: Cup or Chalice of Spring Water Source / Sol (Center): Fire, Yellow or White Candle Petition – You can petition Venus, the planetary ruler of Taurus, to attract what you desire: love, relationships, and physical objects. Venus can help with beauty, the arts, and being more social. Venus gifts attraction, love, beauty, and sociability. Venus is associated with abundance, prosperity, and attracting what you desire. In Taurus, she also represents values and can help you build a life that aligns with your deepest desires. Venus also governs sensuality, beauty, love and relationships, making her an excellent ally for attracting love and connection in all areas of life. Consider calling upon Venus to help you manifest your goals and bring more abundance, prosperity, and fulfillment into your life. One suggested ritual for the Taurus new moon is to manifest abundance. What is abundance? heading: Taurus Season: Taurus/Scorpio Polar Axis
body: The Taurus/Scorpio axis is a powerful combination of energy that invites us to explore the balance between our material possessions and our deeper, emotional needs. As the Taurus and Scorpio energies intertwine, you are called to delve into the delicate balance between your material possessions and your deeper, emotional needs. The Taurus energy, ruled by Venus, reminds you of the importance of material comfort, stability, and abundance. It beckons you to take a moment to reflect on the value of your possessions, and how you can use them to cultivate more prosperity in your life. While Scorpio energy, ruled by Pluto, invites you to delve into the deeper, more intense, and transformative aspects of yourself. It reminds you of the importance of emotional and spiritual depth and encourages you to transform your inner self for greater growth. This powerful axis is a call for you to find a balance between your physical and emotional needs, to honor both your material comfort and your emotional well-being. To navigate this balance, it's important to take a holistic approach, by taking care of yourself in all aspects of your life. As Taurus season unfolds, you are invited to navigate the polarity between the grounded and practical Taurus and the magnetic and mysterious Scorpio. Taurus, the ruler of the second house, offers you insights on money, talent, values, and self-worth. It reminds you to be mindful of your resources and to use them to create abundance and prosperity in your life. On the other hand, Scorpio, ruler of the eighth house, takes you on a journey to understand loss, the unknown, other people's money, and obsession. It invites you to delve deeper into the darker aspects of your life and to embrace the unknown and the transformative power it holds. This polarity between Taurus and Scorpio is a call for you to find balance and harmony between your practical needs and your emotional and spiritual needs. It is also a call for you to navigate your own power, and how you use it in relation to others. Let yourself honor both the tangible and the intangible, as you explore the depths of the self and the occult mysteries. As you navigate through these natural polarities during Taurus season, you may encounter themes such as love vs. obsession, inner resources vs. outer resources, debt vs. abundance, sensual femininity vs. intimate sexuality, groundedness vs. the unknown, wickedness vs. beauty, and trauma vs. nurturance. These are just a few of the many themes that may arise during this time. As the Taurus and Scorpio energies intertwine, you are called to confront the delicate balance between your material and your emotional needs. This axis invites you to assess whether your possessions and financial security are truly serving you or holding you back. It beckons you to let go of anything that is no longer serving your highest good and embrace a deeper sense of transformation and growth. This is a powerful time for you to reassess your priorities, and to ask yourself what truly brings you a sense of security and fulfillment. It is a call for you to honor both your material comfort and your emotional well-being to find a balance that serves you best. As you navigate the Taurus and Scorpio energies, this axis shines a light on the importance of trust and commitment in your relationships, whether they be romantic or platonic. Taurus, being an earth sign, values stability and security, while Scorpio, a water sign, values depth and intensity. Finding a balance between these two energies can lead to strong, committed relationships that stand the test of time. It's an opportunity for you to reflect on the role that material possessions and financial security play in your life and your relationships, and whether they truly serve you or hold you back. It also invites you to explore your deeper emotional needs, and to consider how they play a role in your overall sense of balance and fulfillment. Trust in the natural flow of the universe and in the beauty of the present moment as you navigate this Taurus/Scorpio axis and look within to find deeper understanding of yourself and your relationships. Scorpio Full Moon: Letting Go Of Dead Energies Every full moon gifts us the ability to release. The specifics are colored by the astrological events involved. Every full moon brings light to our deepest shadows, so we can review and release what is no longer energetically supporting our spiritual journey. Full moons are high tides of power, amplifying and creative. The full moon is a time to celebrate and harvest our previous new moon intentions; otherwise, the full moon is a time to make energetic adjustments to align ourselves to call in our intentions. The full moon is a time of celebration and gathering. We sync to the cycle with community, nature, and Spirit. We gather to clear energy, raise energy, gain clarity, set intentions, process symbols, and connect with nature, the Divine, and our Higher Self. The Scorpio full moon is known as one of the most potent full moons of the year. It is celebrated in the Buddhist tradition in the Festival of Wesak or the Festival of the Buddha; It is a time when the wisdom of Buddha is shared and his teachings and compassion revered. It is a time of regeneration and transformation when we get to take a look at what’s behind that closed door. The full moon is about illuminating that unconscious and that which is unseen which is a realm familiar to dear Scorpio. They also highlight polarities, and in this case, it’s the polarity between grounded Taurus and magnetic Scorpio. With the focus on these two natural oppositions, the themes we are working through our love vs obsession, inner resources vs outer resources, debt vs abundance, sensual femininity vs intimate sexuality, groundedness vs the unknown, wickedness vs beauty, and trauma vs nurturance. Of course, it doesn’t stop there, but these are a few of the issues that might arise now, and navigating through the deep Scorpionic waters will take some effort. As the Scorpio energy intensifies, it shines a light on the darker aspects of human nature, illuminating that which you often struggle to see. Scorpio is known for magnifying unseemly behaviors such as sexual exploitation, abuse of power, greed, and manipulation, and brings attention to the root of inequalities and injustices. But Scorpio is not only about exposing these negative traits, it is also about transformation and uncovering hidden truths in order to evolve and grow. This is a powerful time for you to confront your own darkness and look at yourself in the mirror to make the changes you need to make for your own good and the good of others. Scorpio energy invites you to question your values, beliefs, and morals and be willing to challenge them. It reminds you that true power and wisdom come from embracing your vulnerability and authenticity and not becoming lost in the pursuit of greed and manipulation. Scorpio, being a water sign, is known for having an emotional and sensitive nature. Rejection or dismissal can be difficult for this energy to process, especially if Scorpio feels this rejection is unwarranted, or if they have invested a lot of themselves and their time into a situation. Scorpio energy tends to prefer building upon what has already been established rather than starting from scratch, which can make it challenging for this energy to let go of toxic patterns and embrace change. However, Scorpios ultimately learns the importance of letting go of things that no longer serve a purpose; to establish a stable foundation, a priority for Scorpio as a fixed sign. Scorpio isn’t all doom and gloom and offers many gifts through which it bestows wisdom and insight. In its highest form, Scorpio demands the highest level of integrity, and seeks out all that is not serving the higher good of all, and only serving the needs of the self. The purpose of its sharp focus and keen perception is to serve others by leading them through transformation, from darkness into light, from pain into joy, and from oppressiveness to liberation. His ultimate goal is empowerment for the collective good. Scorpio’s techniques aren’t always sensitive or welcoming. He doesn’t coddle or find soft ways to deliver his lessons. He’s focused, to the point, and shows us our weaknesses so that we can learn to stand on our own two feet even when it feels like the rug is being pulled out from under us. So we can realize that nothing is permanent and learn to become comfortable in the uncertainty of life. All of us have been learning to do this over the past several months. Much of the Covid-19 pandemic experience has been Scorpionic. We entered into a completely new terrain that no one has navigated before, and we did our best to take care of ourselves and our families and communities. We experienced a transformation on a global and personal level that has forced us to look at weak areas in our own lives and in government institutions. Scorpio is also indicative of having access to the resources of others. In this case, we see that many need government support, and can see how our government is able or unable to show up. Under the illuminating presence of the full moon in Scorpio, we are likely to discover a fresh dimension of transformation that has the potential to steer us toward an amplified sense of personal empowerment. The recent months have seen a lot of us slip deeper into financial obligations, creating a chaotic whirlpool that now requires our focused attention to restore balance and order. At this juncture, it's important to pause and contemplate how your self-perceptions intertwine with the reality you are experiencing. It's time to question whether your self-love and self-esteem are robust enough to catalyze changes that truly mirror your values and worthiness. Are you embracing your deservingness to receive the goodness life has to offer? Persistently pose this question to yourself, especially during the challenging phases that might occur over the upcoming weeks. Embrace these moments of introspection, for they are opportunities for you to foster self-awareness and personal growth. Continue to present yourself as your own biggest supporter, never failing to show up when you need to, and relentlessly scrutinizing ways in which you can better align with your inner wisdom and guidance. As the Scorpio full moon ushers in intense awakening and transformation. Embrace this time, for it is crucial, though not always comfortable. However, comfort has never been Scorpio's calling card; instead, it pushes us into the depths of transformative growth and self-discovery. This period represents an opportunity to redefine and reshape your vision, crafting a path that leads to enhanced self-empowerment. It's a journey of self-realization, and just as the Scorpio delves into the deep, dark waters, so must we delve into our own inner depths to discover our strengths and potential. In the crucible of this time, we have seen the birth of unprecedented creativity and ingenious solutions. We eagerly anticipate the manifestation of these gifts that are the fruits of our collective imagination, promising to bring about positive change in the near future. Let us extend our hope that these resources and the support accompanying them find their way to the less fortunate among us. The value of our collective achievements is truly realized when shared and utilized for the betterment of all. The structures that we're beginning to implement are more than just temporary fixes. They are critical movements aiming to confront and rectify the deep-seated inequalities and lack of support that have been ignored for far too long. Let these changes not just address, but also uproot, the systemic problems to build a more equitable, inclusive society. As you navigate this transformative phase, may you find the clarity that you seek and the courage to reinvent your life. Just like the Phoenix, Scorpio's archetype, let this time of change be your rebirth, your opportunity to rise resiliently from the ashes, ready to embrace your new reality with open arms.

I use a 7-card spread as a framework, and if there are other significant planetary movements, ex: Mercury Rx, I’ll extend the spread accordingly. Begin by creating two piles. First, separate the Major Arcana cards into a separate pile from the Court and Minor Arcana cards from the Golden Eclipse tarot deck or another of your favorite tarot decks. Second, select the tarot cars from the Major Arcana pile that corresponds to the current planetary places. For example, during Taurus Season, the sun is in Taurus (The Heirophant), opposite the Moon (High Priestess) in Scorpio (Death). As you embrace this full moon's transformative energy, you may find yourself becoming more self-aware and seeing yourself in a whole new light. This is an opportunity to let go of old patterns and habits that no longer serve you, and focus on new beginnings. The Tower card in tarot is a reminder that change can come unexpectedly, shaking up our long-held beliefs and patterns. Mars, the planet associated with this card, is the Awakener, bestowing energy and self-expression. Mars is the warrior, determined and focused on his goals, and the Tower represents the transformative power of the universe to break down what is no longer serving us. This is an opportunity to let go of old ways of being and open ourselves up to new possibilities and growth. Trust in the transformative power of the Universe and in your own strength to navigate this change. As the Scorpio full moon opposes the Sun in Taurus, you are being called to let go of any limiting beliefs and thoughts that may have held you back, such as a lack of self-worth or feelings of being "too much." It is important to remember that living a small life, or dimming your light to make others comfortable, will only lead to soul-crushing unhappiness.
