heading: Horoscopes & Tarotscopes for the Aquarius full moon
body: n Tarotscopes is a practice of combining tarot cards and astrology with writing personalized horoscopes. There are different techniques you can use to write tarotscopes; I favor selecting tarot cards that correspond to the current planetary placements, mapping the cosmos here on earth. I use a 7-card spread as a framework, and if there is another significant planetary movement, ex: Mercury Rx, I’ll extend the spread accordingly. Begin by creating two piles. First, separate the Major Arcana cards into a separate pile from the Court and Minor Arcana cards from the Golden Eclipse tarot deck or another of your favorite tarot decks. Second, select the tarot cars from the Major Arcana pile corresponding to the current planetary places. For example, during Leo Season, the Sun is in Leo (Strength), opposite the Moon (High Priestess) in Aquarius (The Star). Then find the Sun (Sun), Strength (Leo), High Priestess (Moon), and the Star (Aquarius), and place the Sun in position 1, Strength in position 2, High Priestess in position 3, and the Star in position 4. For positions 5 and 6, find which of your natal houses is being illuminated by the full moon (see below), and select the tarot card that represents the ruling zodiac sign and planet for the house. For example, Aries and Mars rule the 1st house, as Taurus and Venus rule the 2nd house. For the 7th position, select a card from the second pile containing the court cards and the Minor Arcana. Use this placement to gain more insight into how to work with this planetary energy. Tarotscope Key 2. The tarot card corresponds to the zodiac sign the sun is in 4. The tarot card corresponds to the zodiac sign the moon is in 6. The tarot card that corresponds to the planetary ruler of the house 7. The Sun (Sun) 3. The High Priestess (Moon) 5. The tarot card the corresponds to the zodiac ruler of the house that is illuminated or a supporting card from the court or minor arcana pile to represent what you want/need to know more of, ex: a card to represent your love life, career, finances, or general support guidance Ex: The Emperor (Aries) ruler of the 1st house Aquarius (Jan. 20 - Feb. 18) & Aquarius Rising - Full moon in the 1st House The Aquarius full moon is illuminating your 1st house of Self. It's a time to reclaim your power and ability to speak your mind freely, not attaching or being afraid of rebelling against the status quo. This gift you naturally have and continue to grow into each year. You are a freedom fighter, and you not only fight for the ability to live a free life in your truth; you also advocate for those around you to live with the same freedoms. At heart, you are a humanitarian. With this Aquarius full moon's opposition to the Sun in Leo, it is time to align your visionary mind with your heart and spirit; walk your path and speak your mind without letting shame get in the way. This full moon asks that you listen to your intuitive voice, which is distinctive to you. Allow this voice to guide you in creating a unique life to your signature soul frequency. There is a power in living a life that is independent and elevated from external conditioning. Living in your unique truth is your gift to yourself and a gift and example to others. They, too, hold the power to envision a life for themselves that aligns with their signature soul vibration. What has shifted in the past six months, allowing you more space and freedom? Have you let go of external judgment? If you're currently feeling restricted due to the opinions of others, how can you free yourself of this judgment? This Aquarius full moon is an opportunity to be guided for the next six months, to step into your power, and honor what makes you unique and different. Leverage your gifts to elevate you from the masses, stand out, and be recognized for your contributions. Aquarius & Aquarius Rising Tarotscopes Create your tarotscopes for this full moon. Create sacred space, clear your mind and position the cards and see what guidance comes forth: The Sun (Sun) in Leo (Strength) opposite the Moon (High Priestess) in Aquarius (The Star), illuminating the 1st House (The Emperor/Aries), with ruling planet Mars (The Tower). 2. The Emperor (Aries) 7. {extra card} Capricorn (Dec. 22 - Jan. 19) & Capricorn Rising - Full moon in the 2nd House The Aquarius full moon illuminates your 2nd House of Disposable Income and Foundation. Take stock of the financial lessons (positive and negative) you’ve learned these past six months, beginning with the new moon in Aquarius. The Aquarius full moon guides you to rebel against and free yourself from any critical thoughts that sabotage your self-worth and self-esteem. The Aquarius full moon in the second house is a time to reflect on your income and security. A time to re-examine your views on self-worth, feelings of lack, money, finances, debt, and any fears that come up around these themes to be worked through and shifted. You challenge disruption and approve commitment, it’s both a positive trait and your downfall. Sometimes, your ability to defer gratification and commit to long-term goals can have you keeping to a decision that isn’t materializing to its greatest potential. Perhaps you were overpromised? Aquarius energy is futuristic, transcending the now and gaining insight from the future. The 2nd House of Finances and Foundation is ruled by Taurus and corresponds to The Hierophant in the Major Arcana of Tarot. The Hierophant represents structure, consistency, and guidance - all essential elements in achieving financial stability and success. The Hierophant can be considered a mentor or guide, someone with the experience and knowledge to help you navigate the path to success. If you're seeking help setting proper financial goals, it may be beneficial to seek a mentor or financial advisor who can provide direction and assistance. This mentor can help you stay focused by setting clear goals and providing guidance, support, and motivation when things are not going your way. Having someone to rely on can save time and effort, as they can prevent costly mistakes and show you the right way. Take a second look at what you committed to in your investments. Did you commit to a financial decision or stock trade that needs to be reworked or traded due to a market forecast? You may be reassessing how secure you feel financially, and take this time to see what steps you need to take to create more of a supportive foundation and take control of that which is within your own self to make yours. This full moon may also signal a time when you make a sizeable investment in yourself, paying for marriage, a downpayment on a house, or paying for education or further education are some examples. Be mindful if any financial planets, like Venus or Mercury, are retrograde at this time. It is not always possible to avoid making financial plans during a retrograde period. If a decision needs to be acted on at this time, quadruple-check any documents and contracts that need to be signed during a possible unstable cosmic window. The more you commit to yourself in the next six months, the more you’ll see your investments, income, and self-worth grow. Whether you're trying to repair a relationship or just create stronger connections with those around you, it's vital, to be honest, open, and clear about what you want and need. Take the time to listen and be heard, and you'll find that understanding can often lead to healing and building a stronger community. So if you find yourself drawn to intellectual conversations, it's because that's exactly what this full moon is calling for. It's a time to seek out conversations that take you deeper, that challenge you to think differently, and question your beliefs (and what you were taught to believe). Unbalanced relationships that are built by expectation will crumble; as new insights will create breakthroughs. This dynamic will push you toward deeper commitment or further away towards liberation. It's time to forgive and reclaim your power. Being aware of the self-sabotaging behaviors that can hinder your growth and goals is essential. heading: Aquarius Full Moon Ritual
body: “I release everything either known or unknown to me that has been blocking me from receiving, feeling, and walking in my strength and authority. I trust and discover strength in my body, mind, self, and spirit. I call in my power and walk in my strength.” - A prayer for release Fig 66. Top view of an altar to Saturn & Capricorn [ See 'Creating an Altar A Framework for Astrological Magick' for altar suggestions] Place the Kamea for Saturn and your ritual candle(s) for Saturn on the placement for Saturn. Place the World and The Star tarot card on your altar, as well as an offering to Saturn. Ascendant (East): Aries, Fire: Candle, Oil Lantern Midheaven (South): Capricorn, Earth: Salt, Plants, Minerals or Crystals (in illustration pine and black tourmaline) Descendant (West): Libra, Air: Powered or Cone Incense, Feather IC / Lower Heaven (North): Cancer, Water: Cup or Chalice of Spring Water Source / Sol (Center): Fire, Yellow or White Candle Begin by taking a spiritual bath. Similar to how we cleanse and consecrate items for use on the altar, you must also purify your own energy. You bathe and prepare yourself in cleansing and energetic waters — setting yourself apart from the mundane 'ordinary' life. This spiritual bath can strengthen your connection to the natural world and the Universal Divine; by combining water's vibrational power and raising that water's energy with words (prayer), incense, oils, plants (herbs), and intentions. A cleansing can increase well-being and uplifts your spirit by washing away stagnation and negativity. It can remove obstacles that block success in achieving your intentions. A bath can be done in a traditional bath or by standing in a shower (and pouring the prepared spiritual bath water over one's head). Once you have finished your bath, it is time to create a sacred space. As with any spiritual/meditative practice or ritual, turn off your phone and create space to not be disturbed. Choose a ritual area in your home that is ideally free of clutter, distractions, and technology. You can use sage, palo santo, or even incense to smudge the air. You can also pour sea salt around the area, sweep it up, and discard it outside your home. Set the mood with incense, music, and the soothing sound of bells. Cleanse your ritual candle before dressing it with herbs and oils. As you light the incense, focus on your intention, pass the candle and a written manifestation of your desire through the smoke. Speak or read your intention out loud. Lastly, place your letter of intention in the bottom (underneath) of the bowl of water and place the candle inside the bowl (if using a pull-out candle in a glass jar). Light your candle and visualize yourself in the moment of your actualized and realized intention. 1. Find a quiet, distraction-free place to set up your altar. 2. Cleanse and consecrate all the items you will place on your altar using a method such as smoke, Florida Water, or a mixture of water and salt. Make sure to use new, cleansed candles. 3. Place consecrated items representing the four elements on your altar: Earth (crystals, herbs, salt in a dish), Water (small cup or bowl of spring water), Air (incense or feather), and Fire (candle). 4. Choose a candle and cleanse and dedicate it to your intention. 5. Set up an altar for the planetary god, goddess, or deity you petition, using the appropriate color cloth and other relevant items. 6. Ensure your altar is in a fire-safe area, not prone to wind disruptions. 7. Take a spiritual bath to cleanse and prepare yourself for the ritual. 8. Perform your spell or ritual by placing your written petition, the planetary sigil, kamea, or symbol representing the deity in the center of the altar, along with the candle and incense. 9. Pray. Ask for want you want, and feel it from the center of your being. 10. When finished, close down the ritual. Never blow out the candle. If you need to extinguish it, either snuff it out or pinch it out with moistened fingers. If you need to pinch the candle flame, say, "this light is out, but the intention carries on." Whenever you relight the candle, remember the feeling of the energy, and restate your intention. 11. Give Thanks. 12. When you have completed your ritual, appropriately dispose of the items. Methods for Grounding After Ritual Grounding is an important aspect of any magical ritual. It allows you to connect with the earth and release excess energy, helping you return to the mundane world. While not every ritual requires grounding, it can be beneficial if you feel overwhelmed with too much energy after a ritual. Here are some ways to ground yourself: ● Touch the ground physically, such as by walking barefoot. ● Visualize roots growing from your feet into the earth to bring balance. ● Eat or drink something grounding, like a warm meal, tea, or a snack. ● Engage in physical activity like going for a walk or run to dissipate excess energy. Troubleshooting Spell and Ritual Difficulties If you are having trouble with a spell or ritual, it could be due to a lack of focus or energy or because something in your life is blocking the spell – this could be due to past life issues, karmic debt, or negative energy. To address these issues, try using white or purple candles and performing a series of uncrossing baths and rituals on Thursdays (for Jupiter) for 3, 5, 7, or 13 days in a row. This may help to clear any obstacles and allow the spell or ritual to work more effectively. Understanding the Timeline of Ritual and Spell Results It's important to note that although a ritual or spell begins working immediately, you may not see results right away. According to the rule of three, results can take three days, three weeks, or three months to manifest. More extensive rituals may take up to a year to complete. Keep in mind that every situation is different, and results may vary. *** Virgo Season: Aug 23rd - Sept 22nd The 6th House, Ruled by Mercury Being of Service, Self Care and Healthy Boundaries “In the Northern Hemisphere we are entering Autumn. Which represents the natural cycle of slowing down and gathering our resources. Our focus is on preservation and nourishment, as we prepare ourselves to go inward for spiritual introspection. This is our moment to sit in the stillness and let it speak to us” New Moon – Virgo (Ruled by Mercury) Full Moon – Pisces (Ruled by Jupiter Ancient Astrology, Neptune Modern Astrology) Planet – Mercury Day of the Week – Wednesday (ruled by Mercury) Archetype – The Virgin Element – Earth Tarot – The Hermit (Virgo) / The Magician (Mercury) Body – Intestines and colon Affirmation – I am of service. I analyze As the veil of summer lifts and autumn takes hold, the leaves fall from the trees and the air grows crisp, signaling the arrival of Virgo season. The natural cycle of autumn is upon us, a time for slowing down and gathering our resources. We focus on preservation and nourishment as we prepare to go inward for spiritual introspection. The stillness of autumn beckons us to sit and listen, to hear the guidance of the season as it leads us toward the intentions and lessons that will birth the new life we seek. There is a beautiful transformation that takes place in autumn, as the leaves flower and change - showing us the transformational ritual of release. Just as autumn teaches us how to re-prioritize our energies and let go, Virgo teaches us to see what’s not working and course correct; often finding more efficient and compassionate ways of doing things, in the process. As we embrace the season of autumn and the energy of Virgo, may we find peace in the process of slowing down, refining, course-correcting, and releasing. The last few moon cycles have been life-changing for many, unstable and unpredictable, as we've re-organized our inner and outer landscapes. The trials of grief, loss, and the unknown have presented themselves. Still, with each step forward, we gain a deeper understanding of navigating and anchoring ourselves within this new way of being. We leverage the energy of Virgo season and take this time to try to organize and make sense of it all. We look at the truth of what is and sift through what works and what doesn’t. Virgo, the Virgin, is associated with work, service, health, purification, organization, and analytical thinking. These are the qualities we seek to embody as we sift through the truth of what is, examining what works and what doesn't in our lives. This is a time to be detail-oriented and to focus on the minutia, ensuring that all the pieces of the puzzle fit together seamlessly. As the wheels of fate turn and we delve deeper into the mystical realm of Virgo, let us be of service to ourselves and others, let us tend to the gardens of our health and well-being, and let us purify our minds and hearts. May we find clarity and organization in the midst of the chaos, as we continue on our journey of growth and self-discovery. As we welcome the grounding and earth-centered energy of Virgo season, many of us may be feeling a sense of relief after the whirlwind of the past few weeks. We may have been forced to confront uncomfortable truths and realign ourselves as a result, or perhaps we're still grappling with deep heartache and questioning reality. But as the Virgo new moon arrives, we are given the opportunity to reorganize ourselves after the chaos. This is a time to release the toxicity on multiple levels, whether it be negative mental patterns, unhealthy habits, or victim consciousness. Let us embrace the healing power of Virgo's purification and organization, as we move towards a more balanced state of being. Virgo is the sign of organization, efficiency, and self-improvement. This energy encourages us to take a closer look at ourselves and make the necessary changes to live a more fulfilling life. We are called to be of service to ourselves and others, to prioritize our health and well-being, and to purify our minds and hearts. As we embrace the Virgo energy of organization, efficiency, and self-improvement, it's a great opportunity to take a closer look at our habits and rituals. It's a time to evaluate what's working for us and what's not and make necessary changes. Health is a major theme for this Virgo new moon and as we approach it, we may want to take the time out to work through unconscious patterns that are expressing themselves through our physical bodies. We are encouraged to start at the most basic level, by breaking unhealthy addictions, whether it be food, relationships, or work situations. It's a time to take stock of what is not serving us and make the necessary changes to cultivate healthier habits and patterns. The Virgo energy invites us to strengthen the muscle that encourages healthy behaviors such as exercise, eating well, sleeping regularly, and repeating positive affirmations for self-confidence and healing. It's a time to focus on the little things that make a big difference in our overall health and well-being. As we embrace this Virgo energy, let us take the time to tune into our bodies, listen to its needs, and nourish it with the care it deserves. Virgo’s signature is one of general anxiety or lack of self-confidence. During this Virgo season and the Virgo new moon take note of the situations and people in your life that aren’t lifting you up, valuing you, or appreciating you for all that you do. Work and service is also a signature of Virgo, and often self-sacrifice without proper recognition can become a pattern that is ultimately mirroring to us that we do not value ourselves enough. The best tools we can use now are grounding practices such as breathwork, body-centered meditations, torus meditations, walks out in nature, dance, music, Tai Chi, Yoga, or Qi Gong. Anything that helps you find your center and stay connected to your body and your experience so you can navigate the murky waters over the next couple of weeks. Virgo season is a time for slowing down, going inward, self-reflection, creating healthy routines, organizing, and being of service. After all the changes and upsets from these past few months - we now seek stability, to collective ourselves, and re-create a healthy day-to-day structure and routing, through the grounded presence of Virgo season. This is a time of year when we can take a look at the ways in which we give too much of ourselves and are left feeling drained and underappreciated. As these places get highlighted, it gives us the opportunity to reorganize situations to make them work for us, so we aren’t only “being of service” for other people's success or satisfaction. That there is an energetic exchange and balance. Use this season to explore which area in your life you are giving too much of yourself without proper recognition or compensation. Virgo's lessons of patience, contemplation, and observation draw us forward to be more present. Our focus shifts to the small details and building blocks that make up our whole life and future. Virgo Season asks that we who we work with, and what labor, service, and being of service means for us. Virgo asks us to purify and cleanse any toxic habits and re-evaluate our day-to-day routines. As we journey through the celestial landscape of Virgo season, we are called to explore the polarity between Virgo and Pisces. The Virgo/Pisces axis is one of the most challenging and karmic in astrology, as it represents the balance between order and chaos. The energy of Virgo is all about organization, efficiency, and self-improvement, while Pisces's energy is about fluidity, emotions, and intuition. This polarity can manifest as a struggle between our desire for stability and order, and our need to let go and surrender to the flow of life. During this time, we may find ourselves oscillating between feelings of disorganization and organization, as we seek stability within the rise and fall of the emotional waves. As we embrace the energy of the Virgo season, let us strive to find balance and harmony in the midst of life's chaos. By learning to navigate the polarity of the Virgo sun and the full moon in Pisces, we can gain a deeper understanding of ourselves and our place in the world. Let us use this time to purify, organize our inner selves, and create healthy habits and routines which give us a sense of structure and stability, while also allowing for flexibility and adaptability that make it easier to surrender to the flow of the universe.

heading: Virgo Light & Shadow
body: As we move into Virgo season, you are reminded of the importance of service and humility. Virgo is the sign of the Virgin, symbolizing purity, innocence, and a desire to be of service to others. When you are in touch with the evolved Virgo energy, you are able to set healthy boundaries, focus on the details, and use your skills and abilities to help others. However, when you are operating in Virgo's shadow, you may become overly critical and perfectionistic, fixating on the flaws and shortcomings of yourself and others. It's important to remember that Virgo energy is about finding a healthy way to express your need for perfection and attention to detail. By cultivating a sense of humility and a desire to be of service, you can tap into the full potential of our evolved Virgo energy and use it to make a positive impact on your daily routines and rituals. As you navigate the push and pull of Virgo's energy, it's important to be mindful of your motivations and to strive for balance. By finding a healthy balance between your need for perfection and your desire to be of service, you can tap into the full potential of the evolved Virgo energy and become shining examples of the power of Spirit. Un-evolved Virgo energy can be critical, obsessive-compulsive, and focus too heavily on the wrongs of what’s not working. Virgo in her shadow is in the critical details - and her inability allows for life's unpredictability. Be mindful of lingering in the energies of Virgos’ Shadow. In its shadow without a connection to Spirit - un-evolved Virgo energy can create anxiety, and be critical of both themselves and others. At the high end, evolved Virgo energy is altruistic and wants to be of service. ​ ​ ​ Virgo Light / Strength: Being of Service, Humbled Ego, Healthy Boundaries Virgo Shadow / Weakness: Perfectionist, critical, obsessive-compulsive, focus too heavily on the wrongs of what’s not working. Feelings of guilt or inadequacy ​ Virgo Season, The 6th House & Planetary Ruler As the great cosmic wheel turns, we find ourselves entering the realm of Virgo, the sixth sign of the zodiac. The sixth house is a place of health, work ethic, and service, and during Virgo season, we turn our focus to the work at hand. This is a time to organize our day-to-day lives and to create healthy routines and boundaries. It is a time to re-evaluate our work, our labor, and the service we provide to others. Virgo asks us to purify and cleanse ourselves of toxic habits and to embrace the lessons of patience, contemplation, and observation. Virgo is a sign of work and beauty, of the perfection that can be achieved through hard work and attention to detail. Ruled by Mercury, it is associated with health, purification, organization, and analytical thinking. Through the lens of Virgo, Mercury is seen as a microscope, analyzing and processing information through the act of organizing and paying attention to the details. These are the qualities we seek to embody as we prepare ourselves for spiritual introspection and the journey inward. As you turn inward for spiritual introspection, the 6th house asks you to consider your daily routines, habits, and responsibilities. It is a time to evaluate how you take care of yourself and your physical well-being through discipline and organization. This includes your job and the choices you make in your day-to-day life, such as how you care for your physical health and what you wear. If your Sun is located in the 6th house, you may naturally be practical and well-organized. However, if there are negative planets in this house, it could indicate potential health or body issues to be mindful of. Virgo / The Hermit The Hermit is the ninth key of the Major Arcana. On the journey from Strength, the Fool develops a sense of self and learns to master her emotions when faced with external challenges. Now that the Fool has mastered her emotions, the Hermit teaches her to master her Self. In this stage of the journey, she finds out who she is at her core. Planetary Ruler – ☿ Mercury Symbolism – Alone but for a cat that watches her, The Hermit teaches that in order to experience divine light, both silence and seclusion are required. At this point, the kundalini energy has been raised to the top of the mountain — a metaphor for the head, where the third eye and crown chakras are located. The lantern is hidden, held inside her cloak, representing the divine inner light that burns within. Her long hair symbolizes the flow of spiritual energy, while the staff in her hand alludes to the divine kundalini energy that flows through the spine and the corresponding chakras during the awakening process. Astrology – The Hermit corresponds to Virgo and Virgo Season, a time in the Northern Hemisphere at the onset of Autumn, a season representing the natural cycle of slowing down and gathering resources before Winter. The spiritual parallel is also one of preservation and nourishment but in preparation for turning within for a course of spiritual introspection. This is the moment to sit in stillness and allow it to speak to you. Virgo, the 6th sign on the cosmic wheel, is associated with work, service, health, purification, organization, being detail-oriented, and analytical thinking. Virgo asks that you purify and cleanse toxic habits; this is a time for a spiritual fast, a soul cleansing as the whole body enters into prayer. Lessons of patience, contemplation, and observation draw await. Virgo asks you to be more present to details, taking a look at the ways in which you give too much of yourself and are left feeling drained and under-appreciated. Upright Meaning – Introspection, alone time, a need for solitude, enjoying your own company, spiritual mastery, heightened state of awareness, inner guidance, search for truth, search for knowledge, exploring shadow, fasting, introspection for personal and spiritual development, taking space from a situation or person to gain perspective, a meeting with a wise person who aid one's journey, the answers one seeks must be found within Reversed – Isolation, loneliness, rejecting assistance or advice from others, unwillingness to explore new ideas or the deeper meaning, separation, lone wolf, depression, fear and suspicion of society, social anxiety disorder, Anthropophobia

heading: Virgo Season and Virgo New Moon: Actions and Intentions
body: During Virgo season, it's important to focus on being of service and setting healthy boundaries. This is a time for spiritual introspection and for going inward to find guidance and direction. It's also a time to pay attention to the ways in which we may be giving too much of ourselves and feeling drained and unappreciated as a result. As we seek stability and grounding during this season, it's important to practice self-care and to set boundaries that help us to feel nourished and supported. Virgo season is a time to re-evaluate our relationships and work situations and to make sure that we are not giving too much of ourselves without proper recognition or compensation. It's also a time to cultivate patience, contemplation, and observation, and to take the time to appreciate the little details and the bigger picture. Remember to offer kind words of appreciation to yourself and others, and to take the time to create more order and structure in your life. Virgo season and the Virgo new moon is a time to focus on being of service and setting healthy boundaries. Virgo season is a time to slow down, go inward, and do the work of processing our emotions and examining our inner landscape. During this time, you may want to reflect on questions such as: How do I balance being of service with taking care of myself? Where do I need to set boundaries in my life? How can I better align my actions with my values and goals? How can I create more order and structure in my life? How can I cultivate patience, contemplation, and observation? I am grounded and centered, taking care of my physical, mental, and emotional well-being. I am organized and efficient, creating flow and balance in my life. I am self-aware and self-analyzing, constantly seeking self-improvement and growth. I am of service to others but also prioritize my own needs and boundaries. I am disciplined and committed to my goals, working hard and consistently towards my dreams. I am open to change and willing to adapt, always striving for excellence and perfection. Create an altar – During Virgo season it is a good time to create a sacred space for Mercury, the planetary ruler of Virgo. To create an altar, you can gather items that have personal meaning or significance to you. You might also collect items that symbolize Mercury and Virgo. Set up the altar in a space where you can sit and reflect, and take the time to meditate or journal in this space. Observe – Observe and record any symbolisms or messages that you notice during this full moon. A journal is like a magick portal to your innermost thoughts and dreams. Every page is an invitation to explore, reflect, and express yourself in a meaningful way. Collect items – Grab a pen, paper, candles, incense, herbs, and symbolic objects to represent Mercury/Virgo, like The Magician, The Hermit tarot cards, and the Planetary Kamea for Mercury. Cultivate healthy boundaries that protect and respect your energy – This might involve setting limits on your time and energy, saying no to commitments that drain you or taking care of your physical and emotional needs. Tap into your instincts and trust your inner wisdom – This might involve spending time in nature, meditating, or journaling to connect with your inner self. Make a list – Collect and organize your thoughts, and take time to analyze and reflect on them. This can be a helpful way to gain clarity and focus. Organize – Take time to organize your space and protect your energy. Be mindful of who you share your energy and resources with, and consider what boundaries you need to set in order to feel grounded and centered. Self-Care – Focus on optimizing your daily hygiene, dressing tidily, and being clean. Take care of your body by nourishing it with healthy, colon-supportive foods like oatmeal. Remember to prioritize self-care. Virgo New Moon: Cultivating Personal Growth We’ve moved past Leo season and now we’ve entered the season of Virgo. The last few months have been life-changing for many. Unstable and unpredictable as we’ve been reorganizing both our inner and outer landscapes. Learning to navigate grief, loss, change, and newness. We leverage the energy of Virgo season and take this time to try to organize and make sense of it all. We look at the truth of what is, and sift through what works and what doesn’t. Our focus shifts to the small details that make up our whole life. Virgo is associated with work, service, health, purification, organization, being detail-oriented, and analytical thinking. These are the qualities we want to embody during this Season. In the Northern Hemisphere, we are entering Autumn. Which represents the natural cycle of slowing down and gathering our resources. Our focus is on preservation and nourishment, as we prepare ourselves to go inward for spiritual introspection. This is our moment to sit in the stillness and let it speak to us, let it guide us to the intentions and lessons that must birth the new life we are seeking. There is a beautiful transformation that takes place in Autumn, as the leaves flower - and show us the transformational ritual of release. Just as Autumn teaches us how to release; Virgo pushes us to see what’s not working and course correct, often finding more efficient and compassionate ways of doing things, in the process. Virgo is the ultimate Sacred Mother. The Goddess of Purity and Innocence. The Virgin. Think of Mother Theresa. She’s selfless, caring, compassionate, and endlessly working towards the betterment of humankind and serving those less fortunate than herself. In this way, Virgo is associated with work, service, health, purification, organization, and detail-oriented, analytical thinking. These are the qualities we want to embody during this time. Any place we feel small, unworthy, or neglected will show us exactly where we need to be doing our own inner work. This new moon is pushing us forward on our healing path, an internal reworking and releasing of old stuck patterns and victimization. When we face, heal, and accept these parts of ourselves, we realize that nothing can stop us from achieving our dreams. Virgo forces us to focus on the details, the grit, and the practical steps we need to take to move forward; good things come with consistent effort, a solid foundation, and the right timing. Virgo pushes us to see what’s not working and course correct, often finding more efficient and compassionate ways of doing things. Of course, we can’t speak of Virgo without acknowledging its dark side as well. Within the theme of purification and organization, Virgo has a tendency to seek out perfection, which is of course unattainable. Yet, convincing someone with a strong Virgo influence in their birth chart of this can be quite challenging. To gain insight into this dynamic, we can explore Virgo's polarity, which is Pisces. A valuable lesson for Virgo is learning to assert boundaries. Emerging from the boundary-less nature of Pisces, Virgo now embraces the practice of setting boundaries and prioritizing self-care. During this Virgo season and the arrival of the Virgo new moon, we have an opportunity to examine instances where we extend ourselves excessively, resulting in feelings of exhaustion and underappreciation. These instances serve as beacons, urging us to reevaluate our circumstances and transform them into situations that support our well-being, rather than solely serving others' success or contentment. By relinquishing toxic and unproductive situations, we can achieve significant progress, inviting greater ease, efficiency, and acknowledgment into our lives. As we navigate this transformative phase, let us recognize Virgo's capacity to identify areas for improvement and course correction. Simultaneously, we acknowledge the pursuit of perfection that may bring forth challenges. Embracing Virgo's lessons, we cultivate the ability to say "No" when necessary, establish healthy boundaries, and practice self-care. This period of introspection and alignment during the Virgo season and under the influence of the Virgo new moon empowers us to reorganize our lives, harnessing our energy for personal fulfillment rather than solely focusing on the needs of others. By relinquishing toxic dynamics, we create an environment characterized by enhanced flow, efficiency, and recognition. Virgo brings a sense of order to the ineffable chaos of Pisces. Virgo attempts to ground and manifest the perfection of the Piscean oneness and beauty. But the nature of Pisces is elusive and intangible, thus impossible to live up to its unrealistic ideals and expectations. When looking for what’s not working and trying to make it work in some idea of “perfection” that Virgo has in mind, an unrelenting critic rears its ugly head. This creates stress and conflict internally for Virgo, and also for those around them who may feel that they can never do anything “right.” Our health, our work, and the stress of perfection, or imperfection, are major themes for all of us now. The stress of this constant tension to manifest perfection can leave one feeling unworthy and guilt-ridden as they respond to any of their behavior or facet of their being which they view as imperfect. This stress is often internalized and can create health issues when left unchecked. Suffering through physical issues is often connected to those with strong Virgo in their chart. There are several ways to best make use of this energy. One is to go out in Nature. Virgo is ruled by Mercury, and is heavily focused on mental energy and thoughts, Virgo is after all an Earth sign. There is no better way to experience and witness perfection than to connect with the beauty and perfection of Nature. When you think of Virgo in Nature, think of fractals, spirals, the intricacy and sacred geometry of plants and water molecules, colors, sounds, and the expansiveness of the universe. All that is beyond our comprehension, yet makes us feel connected, interconnected, to the oneness that is Nature, that is Pisces. Here we can appreciate all the imperfections and see just how perfect it all is. Here we can relax and reconnect to ourselves in a new and more accepting way. Virgo can easily focus on what’s not working - be mindful to reframe your focus, as to not steal from the progress you have made. From a detached observer’s perspective - go through what is and isn’t working, in all systems of your life. By the time Virgo season ends, your life will have been reorganized - and the lessons of learning to love yourself and others for all our imperfections learned.

heading: Horoscopes & Tarotscopes for the Virgo new moon
body: Tarotscopes is a practice of combining tarot cards and astrology to write personalized horoscopes. There are different techniques you can use to write tarotscopes; I favor selecting tarot cards that correspond to the current planetary placements, mapping the cosmos here on earth. I use a 6-card spread as a framework, and if there is another significant planetary movement, ex: Mercury Rx, I’ll extend the spread accordingly. Begin by creating two piles. First, separate the Major Arcana cards into a separate pile from the Court and Minor Arcana cards from the Golden Eclipse tarot deck or another of your favorite tarot decks. Second, select the tarot cards from the Major Arcana pile corresponding to the current planetary places. For example, during the Virgo new moon, the sun (Sun) and moon (High Priestess) are in Virgo (The Hermit). Begin by finding the Sun (Sun), High Priestess (Moon), and then The Hermit (Virgo). For positions 5 and 6, find which of your natal houses is being illuminated by the new moon (see below), and select the tarot card that represents the ruling zodiac sign and planet for the house. For example, Aries and Mars rule the 1st house, as Taurus and Venus rule the 2nd house. For the 6th position, select either a card representing your sun sign or a card from the second pile, which contains the court cards and the Minor Arcana; use this placement to gain more insight into how to work with this planetary energy. The Virgo new moon is illuminating your 1st house of self. It’s time to focus on new beginnings and releasing old unhealthy patterns. Taking some time for self-care is always a good idea, but under your new moon, your desire to purify and heal your body and life is amplified. Focus on how you see yourself rather than how others see you. Take the time to reflect and really understand yourself, your needs and wants, and your values. Break out of the cycle of guilt-driven productivity and overconsumption - self-care is key to a healthier mental state. Take time for yourself each day to restore and reflect. Spend time in nature or practice yoga, write in a journal or meditate. Whatever works for you, make sure to schedule it into your day so that it becomes a regular habit. Some decision you made about 6 months ago is now up for review and revision. Think about all that has transpired since then. Try not to allow any disappointments or grief to keep you from moving forward. You’re focused on yourself, your health, and what you need to do to make your desires a reality, and in doing so you may be in opposition to some important relationships in your life. Virgo corresponds to The Hermit. The Hermit is willing to explore the shadows and bring what is hidden into the light. The Hermits' lessons bring you to wholeness and authenticity. With the Virgo new moon in the 1st house, this is a time to step firmly into your power, cultivating a healthy self-image and personal responsibility. The 1st house is ruled by Aries and corresponds to The Emperor in the Major Arcana. The Emperor guides you to take control of your own worth and value, painting a picture of yourself that comes from within - beyond any external, socially defined norms. Let this be a reminder that you can be your own source of wisdom, recognition, and strength. The New Moon in Virgo is a time to clarify what you want to call in, what talents you want to develop, and which direction you want to take in life. If you have experienced setbacks this past year, this is the time to strategize on how to face and solve any challenges. With a New Moon in your sign, it’s time to focus on new beginnings and releasing old unhealthy patterns. This is a time of rebirth and redirection. The Emperor (Aries) Leo (July 23 - Aug. 22) & Leo Rising - New moon in the 2nd House The Virgo new moon illuminates your 2nd house of disposable income and Foundation. The magick is in healthy day-to-day rituals and steps on your path toward financial health. Thoughts shift to letting go of critical ideas that sabotage your self-worth and self-esteem. The more you commit to your health and establish a healthy day-to-day routine, the more you'll see your investments and income growth in the next six months. Set your goals and stay committed to them. Sometimes it feels like you're stuck in a never-ending cycle of planning and waiting. But remember that even if you can't see the manifestation of your goals yet, your hard work and dedication will eventually pay off. There’s been a lot of activity in your sign over the last month, and you are emerging with a new sense of who you are and what direction you want to take. Any behind-the-scenes work you’ve been doing will soon be noticed. How much you value yourself is apparent in what you’re manifesting externally. Keep showing up for yourself and believing in your talents; your beauty, your compassion, and creativity will be seen. This month is about reconnecting to your resources, finances, security, and self-worth. Taking time to realign your values is critical to your emotional well-being. You often struggle with feeling secure, so this time gives you the courage to affirm your sense of worth and value. Honoring your values, reworking your finances, and exploring your senses and sensuality is most important to you now. The second house corresponds to The Hierophant in Major Arcana. The Hierophant teaches that there is more than just the material world; there is a divine ruler. As the High Priestess taught the Fool to discover spiritual wisdom from within, the Hierophant teaches the Fool to find spiritual wisdom from external sources: Spiritual leaders, mentors, ancestors, and community. The Hierophant's links to religion, knowledge, and traditions passed down through oral teachings parallel the "fixed" teachings that comprise our social and religious framework. The Hierophant guides you to return to tradition; you may have expanded your horizons past your comfort zone, and now it's time to return to the familiar to re-frame your focus. The Hierophant is often seen as embodying structure and consistency— two powerful ingredients in achieving success and financial stability. Think of the Hierophant as your guide or mentor — someone who has the experience and knowledge to get you on the path to success. Your mentor can help you stay focused by helping you set clear goals and providing guidance, support, and motivation when things aren’t going your way. By having a mentor or financial advisor to lean on, you can save time and effort because instead of making costly mistakes along the way, you’ll have someone there to show you the right way. So if you’re looking for help in setting up proper financial goals, perhaps it's time to seek out a Hierophant-type figure who can provide much-needed direction and assistance. Communication can sometimes be challenging for your shy and reclusive nature. You worry about speaking properly or not being understood. If confusion arises, make every effort to show up and find ways to bridge the communication gap and create understanding. Words are limiting but hold great power when directed with kind intentions; Communication, perspective shifts, and information are streaming into you and swirling around you now. This is a good week to celebrate any of your siblings' and social-media accomplishments (especially if you're in marketing). This is also a good time to communicate and clear up any misunderstandings or falling-outs you may have had with your siblings. The third house is ruled by Gemini (The Lovers) and Mercury (The Magician) as its planetary ruler. The Lovers and The Magician allude to the magick and power of connections. If you're fortunate enough to have your needs met and still have the capacity to give back, then why not share it with your local community? Home is where the heart is, and your heart is speaking loudly to you now. Who, where, and what are you giving your heart to in the present and the past. You may be feeling more reclusive during this New Moon, but it’s helping you get clear on your own internal emotional process. Unlike your usual social nature, you may feel like being alone now, tending to the illusions or misinformation that has been revealed at work or at home. You may also be seeing some changes surrounding home/family right now, or be thinking about moving and exploring the various contradictions and conflicts within yourself around what you need to feel happy and stable. What does home mean to you? To some, it is the foundation that grounds and sustains their families. To others, it is a place of refuge, security, and comfort. To many, it’s their sanctuary away from the toils of the world. This could be a great time to take stock of your home and make certain changes to suit your preferences and goals. Ask yourself if the location still aligns with what you want for yourself and your family. If a change is in order, then start planning carefully and strategically as there may be positive material rewards in it for you. This may also be a time when your emotional needs are being renegotiated. All relationships require give and take. The 4th house is ruled by Cancer and corresponds to The Chariot in the Major Arcana. You appreciate attention to the details when it comes to all these things, and now could be a time when you bring your vision to reality. Intense feelings about your own worth and value may cause temporary emotional conflict. Returning to an old hobby or joyful pastime can help lift your mood. It’s important for you to stay connected to what you love. The 5th house is ruled by Leo and corresponds to Strength in the Major Arcana. The Strength card reminds you of a sacred power, grounded in inner strength and trust, that comes from emotional mastery. The Strength card of the Golden Eclipse tarot illustrates the Fool sitting poised, channeling the energy of the Universe. The lion is a metaphor for the primal energies of the emotional body, the flames referencing its burning passions. Strength symbolizes being in tune with your inner creative flow when time seems to stand still. It symbolizes the power of channeling Source. When you focus on creating from a place of pure presence, you can tap into a field of awareness that unlocks all the infinite possibilities of creation. With the new moon activating your 6th house, this is a time to introduce activities that can help you channel energy toward better health. Running is a great way to do this, as it increases blood circulation to the brain, improving your mood. Running and walking can also be forms of meditation, connecting your mind and body, clearing your mind, and keeping you present in the moment, which can help reduce anxiety. The 6th house is ruled by Virgo and corresponds to The Hermit in the Major Arcana. The Hermit teaches you to master the Self by practicing silence, meditation, and seclusion. In this stage of the journey, you're being asked to be more attentive to details, looking at how you give too much of yourself and are left feeling drained and under-appreciated. Your New Moon intention is, “To tend to yourself first so that you can better serve others. Slow down and focus on the details of health, work, and daily habits. You live in the sea of bliss and creative inspiration and when it comes to relationships sometimes reality can feel too overwhelming or messy. Tend to what’s not working in your relationships by communicating, focusing on reciprocity, and remembering that being human is a part of life, not something to avoid or judge. Relationships in work and love are at the forefront for you now. Any issues and imbalances that haven’t been dealt with, will finally arise for resolution, or at least discussion. Face the fears that are coming up around commitment or abandonment and work through them with support. Be honest about what you need from others and yourself. Honesty is a liberating act. Not everyone in your life is going to be able to receive what you have to give. And that's okay. Just be conscious of what you expect from others, and be wary of wanting what they can't give and giving what they can't receive. Some people only know how to take, and others know how to receive. Be grateful for those who can welcome you with open hearts. Healthy relationships genuinely are the secret source to a life well lived. Libra rules the 7th house and corresponds to Justice in the Major Arcana. Justice wants you to find clarity, emotional balance, and fairness in relationships. Sometimes it's easier to be more compassionate to those in your intimate relationship than yourself. Give yourself the same emotional support you would give another. The Virgo new moon is giving you the opportunity to make necessary changes to help you evolve as a person and as a partner. Your New Moon intention is, “The other is a reflection of your own inner beauty and inner darkness. Both are part of the Infinite Love and are necessary to be accepted to become whole. To tend to your heart in relationship matters, and trust in the cycles of endings and beginnings.” Pisces & Pisces Rising Tarotscopes Create your tarotscopes for this new moon. Your natural tendency is to bolt when things get tough, though you have a deep sense of loyalty in you. Themes of trust, manipulation, deepening or widening intimacy, and shared resources are consuming you now. Know your value, and don’t allow yourself to be swayed into something that doesn’t feel right. It’s a time of transformation and trust in the unfolding of life. Areas of Intimacy and shared resources are your focus as you learn to trust in yourself most of all. Power dynamics may force you to look inside yourself and access that well of inner power and strength you may not have known you have. Step to that edge of discomfort, and let go of that small version of yourself. Don’t fear what you might transform into. You are much more expansive and empowered than you realize, and being in connection with another may remind you of this whether it’s birthed out of a deep connection, or a lesson of disempowerment. Power dynamics that haven’t been addressed are now arising asking for changes in your relationships. You may come face to face with how much you subconsciously depend on others to feel validated. Any unhealthy or abusive behaviors within yourself or from others need to be let go of. The 8th house is ruled by Scorpio and corresponds to Death in the Major Arcana. The New moon in the eighth house can represent a 'death' from one's old Self or old life and a drastic and necessary change in lifestyle. Getting caught up in internal thoughts and life's battles is easy. But if you take a moment to create a tiny altar in your space, it can help you remember what's important and where to focus your attention. The new moon in the 8th house signals a time of transformation. Some are big and noticeable, while others are small and more personal. But all of these transformations require you to let go of your old self and embrace the destiny meant for you. Your intention for this New Moon is “Security is an inner construct that you have some control over. Build trust in yourself and trust outside yourself will naturally follow. Even in the darkness, I find the light and power I hold within. Open to the fears arising and tune into what is a fear-based decision vs an intuitive gut decision. Trust yourself first, and everything else will align.” Aquarius & Aquarius Rising Tarotscopes Create your tarotscopes for this new moon. Death (Scorpio/8th) Capricorn (Dec. 22 - Jan. 19) & Capricorn Rising - New moon in the 9th House The Virgo new moon illuminates your 9th house of the higher self. Traveling and travelers are active in your reality right now and creating a perspective shift on how you approach your life. Taking a break from the daily grind is a great idea and allows you to refocus on what’s important to you. Sometimes change can be difficult for you, but now’s a time for you to stretch past your comfort zone and broaden your horizons. Keep your mind open to new perspectives, and new worlds begin to open up. You crave an expansive life, where you can venture beyond your own four walls and find something new. There’s no denying the tug of wanderlust. Successful exploration requires inner preparation and thoughtfulness. You need the courage to push past fear, the conviction to follow your heart even, and intuition and learn from them. The 9th house is ruled by Sagittarius and corresponds to Temperance in the major arcana. Temperance symbolizes the merging of the spiritual and mundane worlds. On a spiritual level, Temperance speaks of the potential for genuine communication with your Higher Self. It is a moment of spiritual transformation. Temperance symbolizes the merging of the spiritual and mundane worlds. Your intention for this New Moon is “How can I reconnect to my sense of purpose and spirituality so I can plan my path?” Capricorn & Capricorn Rising Tarotscopes Create your tarotscopes for this new moon. Create sacred space, clear your mind and position the cards and see what guidance comes forth: The Sun (Sun) and Moon (The High Priestess) are in Virgo (The Hermit), illuminating the 9th House (Sagittarius/Temperance), with the ruling planet Jupiter (Wheel of Fortune). For the 6th position, place your Sun sign, Capricorn (The Devil), and/or one card from the Minor Arcana to give you further insight. 3. The Hermit (Virgo) 1. The Sun (Sun) 5. Wheel of Fortune (Jupiter) 2. The High Priestess (Moon) 4. Temperance (Sagittarius/9th house) 6. The Devil (Capricorn) {extra card} Sagittarius (Nov. 22 - Dec. 21) & Sagittarius Rising - New moon in the 10th House The Virgo new moon illuminates your 10th house of career and purpose. You can be perpetually young, but new responsibilities have been put in front of you. At some point, you will need to make some mature decisions because your choices affect those around you. In the last few weeks, you may have been experiencing difficulty, and setbacks at work causing stressors or physical ailments – but this new moon brings relief; as a particular relationship in your life can provide support to help you navigate your way out of this challenging work situation. Your work and status are up for review now. Perhaps where you thought you were going isn’t exactly working out and your plan needs revision. Or if you’ve landed a dream job, make sure all the details are clear. Career is your main focus now. You’re discovering more and more about yourself on a daily basis and wondering if all the different parts of yourself are being honored and acknowledged in your work. This question might eventually lead you to take on a new career path, or maybe even a promotion. You don’t always like being in leadership roles, but now you’re seeing that taking on some extra responsibility, whether that be in your current work, or forging a path on your own, is a necessary step to feeling fulfilled. The 10th house is ruled by Capricorn and corresponds to the Devil in the Major Arcana. The Devil/Capricorn speaks to any false belief that you are trapped or stuck in your current circumstances. The Devil/Capricorn reminds you that you have agency in your life and that no matter your current circumstances, you have the power and magick to create change. Your intention for this New Moon is, settling down doesn’t mean getting stuck in a routine, an eternal state of complacency. It's about understanding your needs and anchoring yourself into acts that bring lifetime fulfillment. Sagittarius & Sagittarius Rising Tarotscopes Create your tarotscopes for this new moon. Create sacred space, clear your mind and position the cards and see what guidance comes forth: The Sun (Sun) and Moon (The High Priestess) are in Virgo (The Hermit), illuminating the 10th House (Capricorn/The Devil), with ruling planet Saturn (The World). For the 6th position, place your Sun sign, Sagittarius (Temperance), and/or one card from the Minor Arcana to give you further insight. 3. The Hermit (Virgo) 1. The Sun (Sun) 5. The World (Saturn) 2. The High Priestess (Moon) 4. The Devil (Capricorn/10th house) 6. Temperance (Sagittarius) {extra card} Scorpio (Oct. 23 - Nov. 21) & Scorpio Rising - New moon in the 11th House The Virgo new moon illuminates your 11th house of friendship. You desire deep connection in every aspect of your life. Your friendships and community, bring you a source of inspiration that you’ve been seeking. However, try not to get ahead of yourself with lofty goals, or disappointment will set in, and trust will need to be mended once again. The right use of power will always be a theme in your life. Friends, community, and networking with others is changing and opening for you. See where your gifts can be offered and offer them. The 11th house is ruled by Aquarius (The Star) with planetary rulers Saturn (The World) and Uranus (The Fool). The Star symbolizes one's wish granted, as it rules over the Law of Attraction. Whatever you put your intention towards, you can bring into your reality. If you are looking to be discovered and seen for your art and talents - now is the time to take action and set those intentions. This starts with being intentional with your thoughts, feelings, and who you surround yourself with. If you are an artist: writer, musician, artist, actor, etc., this is a time to set the intention to have yourself, and your work seen. If you have an established network, use it. If you are starting to build your network and community - put energy into being seen, and discovered for your art and talents. Community and networking is a big focus for you now. Friendships may be changing, and you might find yourself working with groups that are new and different for you. This is good to help you explore new sides of yourself and get exposed to new ideas and visions. Your New Moon intention is, “Stay focused on what’s working in your projects and relationships and gently tend to what’s not working. We build trust with others by committing to outcomes that support the greater good.” Scorpio & Scorpio Rising Tarotscopes Create your tarotscopes for this new moon. Create sacred space, clear your mind and position the cards and see what guidance comes forth: The Sun (Sun) and Moon (The High Priestess) are in Virgo (The Hermit), illuminating the 11th House (Aquarius/The Star), with the ruling planet Uranus (The Fool). For the 6th position, place your Sun sign, Scorpio (Death), and/or one card from the Minor Arcana to give you further insight. 3. The Hermit (Virgo) 1. The Sun (Sun) 5. The World (Saturn) / The Fool (Uranus) 2. The High Priestess (Moon) 6. Death (Scorpio) {extra card} 4. The Devil (Capricorn/10th house) Libra (Sept. 23 - Oct. 22) & Libra Rising - New moon in the 12th House The Virgo new moon illuminates your 12th house of karma, subconscious, and endings. Making decisions doesn’t always come easy for you, Libra, and this aspect of your personality might be amplified now. It might be best not to make important decisions at the moment. Rest, retreat, and focus on connecting with yourself and your creativity so that you can get clear on your purpose. The external world might feel like an overwhelming mess, but this will pass; you’ll be back to your charming self in no time. Dreams, creativity, illusions, and loss are surrounding you now. Clarity may come in time; for now, focus on your creative expression. This New Moon is in your 12th house, the house of the subconscious, karma, endings and home of Pisces. If you feel like you’re underwater, know that this will pass soon, and use this time to connect to your spiritual and artistic side. Let yourself dream, meditate, and be inspired by all that’s coming through to you right now. This energy is more about exploring your internal landscape and expressing it creatively as a manifestation of the divine. You may be receiving downloads of information from past lifetimes or ancestral lineage, trauma that needs to be healed and cleared. Focus on how this makes you feel. You need to move and feel your way through this. Do not try to escape. Use your creative outlet and faith in something higher than yourself to be the path towards healing. Reflect on your purpose and hold it in your heart, regardless of how much suffering surrounds you. The 12th house is ruled by Pisces, with the ancient ruler of Jupiter corresponding to the Wheel of Fortune in the Major Arcana. This cosmic wheel symbolizes the ever-changing cycles of life and the endings that come with them. You can tap into its fortune if you remain aligned with Universal energy but resist it, and you can experience turbulent waters. Life is all about flow, so remember to center yourself within this infinite energy and trust that it will guide you. Your New Moon intention is, “Everything will pass and everything is temporary. For now, set your compass internally and tend to the emotions arising. This is your home and safe space now.” Libra & Libra Rising Tarotscopes Create your tarotscopes for this new moon. Create sacred space, clear your mind and position the cards and see what guidance comes forth: The Sun (Sun) and Moon (The High Priestess) are in Virgo (The Hermit), illuminating the 12th House (Pisces/The Moon), with the ruling planet Neptune (The Hanged Man) or Jupiter (The Wheel of Fortune). For the 6th position, place your Sun sign, Libra (Justice), and/or one card from the Minor Arcana to give you further insight. 3. The Hermit (Virgo) 1. The Sun (Sun) 5. The Hanged Man (Neptune/Modern) / The Wheel of Fortune (Jupiter/Ancient) 2. The High Priestess (Moon) 6. Justice (Libra) {extra card} 4. The Moon (Pisces/12th house) New Moon Ritual Timing The power of manifestation, to give something form. A new cycle. The energy of new possibilities. Time to set your intentions for what you want to bring into your life. Each new moon is a new beginning. With each new beginning, we are asked to release unfinished business, draining distractions from the past - these are required to be neutralized or integrated into the new cycle for a healthy culmination and manifestation. New Moons often mean beginnings and planting new seeds. Write down what you desire to manifest over the next six (6) to eighteen (18) months. Virgo themes include being of service, humbled ego, healthy boundaries, creating a healthy framework to process emotions, and organized manifestation. To align your intentions with the new moon, select a time after the new moon alignment. Not before. Your desire is to have the moon ‘waxing’ / growing as you speak, write, and set your intentions. The most powerful manifesting period is the eight ( 8 ) hour window* that follows the exact new moon alignment. * if you cannot perform your ritual within the first 8 hours. You still have 60 hours after the exact New Moon alignment for manifesting Virgo New Moon Ritual Fig 67. Top view of an altar Mercury & Virgo [ See 'Creating an Altar A Framework for Astrological Magick' for altar suggestions] Place the Kamea for Mercury and your ritual candle(s) for Mercury on the placement for Mercury. Place The Magician & The Hermit tarot cards on your altar, as well as symbols for Virgo & Mercury and offerings to Mercury. Ascendant (East): Aries, Fire: Candle, Oil Lantern Midheaven (South): Capricorn, Earth: Salt, Plants, Minerals or Crystals (in illustration Dill, Cinnamon, Agate) Descendant (West): Libra, Air: Powered or Cone Incense, Feather IC / Lower Heaven (North): Cancer, Water: Cup or Chalice of Spring Water Source / Sol (Center): Fire, Yellow or White Candle Petition – You can petition Mercury to work on your behalf. Mercury rules travel and trade and is the go-between: a door opening. Petition Mercury to open up doors of communication, travel, job seeking/trade, and quick cash. Mercury also rules mental faculties and increased focus, alertness, and luck. Mercury can work with any other influence. A suggested ritual for the Virgo new moon can be to go inwards to heal, create healthy patterns to open up roads and opportunities to “do the work”, and manifest what you desire. Begin by taking a spiritual bath. Similar to how we cleanse and consecrate items for use on the altar, you must also purify your own energy. You bathe and prepare yourself in cleansing and energetic waters — setting yourself apart from the mundane 'ordinary' life. This spiritual bath can strengthen your connection to the natural world and the Universal Divine; by combining water's vibrational power and raising that water's energy with words (prayer), incense, oils, plants (herbs), and intentions. A cleansing can increase well-being and uplifts your spirit by washing away stagnation and negativity. It can remove obstacles that block success in achieving your intentions. A bath can be done in a traditional bath or by standing in a shower (and pouring the prepared spiritual bath water over one's head). Once you have finished your bath, it is time to create a sacred space. As with any spiritual/meditative practice or ritual, turn off your phone and create space not to be disturbed. Choose a ritual area in your home that is ideally free of clutter, distractions, and technology. You can use sage, palo santo, or even incense to smudge the air. You can also pour sea salt around the area, sweep it up, and discard it outside your home. Set the mood with incense, music, and the soothing sound of bells. Cleanse your ritual candle before dressing it with herbs and oils. As you light the incense, focus on your intention, pass the candle and a written manifestation of your desire through the smoke. Speak or read your intention out loud. Lastly, place your letter of intention in the bottom (underneath) of the bowl of water and place the candle inside the bowl (if using a pull-out candle in a glass jar). Light your candle and visualize yourself in the moment of your actualized and realized intention. 1. Find a quiet, distraction-free place to set up your altar. 2. Cleanse and consecrate all the items you will place on your altar using a method such as smoke, Florida Water, or a mixture of water and salt. Make sure to use new, cleansed candles. 3. Place consecrated items representing the four elements on your altar: Earth (crystals, herbs, salt in a dish), Water (small cup or bowl of spring water), Air (incense or feather), and Fire (candle). 4. Choose a candle and cleanse and dedicate it to your intention. 5. Set up an altar for the planetary god, goddess, or deity you petition, using the appropriate color cloth and other relevant items. 6. Ensure your altar is in a fire-safe area, not prone to wind disruptions. 7. Take a spiritual bath to cleanse and prepare yourself for the ritual. 8. Perform your spell or ritual by placing your written petition, the planetary sigil, kamea, or symbol representing the deity in the center of the altar, along with the candle and incense. 9. Pray. Ask for want you want, and feel it from the center of your being. 10. When finished, close down the ritual. Never blow out the candle. If you need to extinguish it, either snuff it out or pinch it out with moistened fingers. If you need to pinch the candle flame, say, "this light is out, but the intention carries on." Whenever you relight the candle, remember the feeling of the energy, and restate your intention. 11. Give Thanks. 12. When you have completed your ritual, appropriately dispose of the items. Methods for Grounding After Ritual Grounding is an important aspect of any magical ritual. It allows you to connect with the earth and release excess energy, helping you return to the mundane world. While not every ritual requires grounding, it can be beneficial if you feel overwhelmed with too much energy after a ritual. Here are some ways to ground yourself: ● Touch the ground physically, such as by walking barefoot. ● Visualize roots growing from your feet into the earth to bring balance. ● Eat or drink something grounding, like a warm meal, tea, or a snack. ● Engage in physical activity like going for a walk or run to dissipate excess energy. Troubleshooting Spell and Ritual Difficulties If you are having trouble with a spell or ritual, it could be due to a lack of focus or energy or because something in your life is blocking the spell – this could be due to past life issues, karmic debt, or negative energy. To address these issues, try using white or purple candles and performing a series of uncrossing baths and rituals on Thursdays (for Jupiter) for 3, 5, 7, or 13 days in a row. This may help to clear any obstacles and allow the spell or ritual to work more effectively. Understanding the Timeline of Ritual and Spell Results It's important to note that although a ritual or spell begins working immediately, you may not see results right away. According to the rule of three, results can take three days, three weeks, or three months to manifest. More extensive rituals may take up to a year to complete. Keep in mind that every situation is different, and results may vary. Exploring Virgo Season and New Moon through Journaling Virgo is the sign of analysis and attention to detail, representing our ability to improve and perfect. During Virgo season or a Virgo full moon, the universe may bring up issues related to your personal growth and self-improvement. You can use tarot as a way to inspire journaling. Select a spread or layout that resonates with your current focus or intention. Shuffle the deck and draw a card, then reflect on its meaning and symbolism. Use the card as a starting point for your journaling and allow its imagery and message to inspire your thoughts and feelings. Explore the card's themes and messages in greater depth and consider how they relate to your experiences and challenges. Reflect on how the card may offer guidance or insights for your current situation and how you can integrate its message into your life. Light a white or green candle and create a peaceful atmosphere by using calming scents and soothing music. Visualize yourself focusing on your personal growth and drawing strength from your own dedication to self-improvement. Take this opportunity to reflect on your own progress and what you can do to continue learning and growing. Open your journal and begin writing about your personal growth and self-improvement. You may also want to consider any challenges or obstacles you have faced in your journey towards self-improvement, and brainstorm ways to overcome them. Remember to be kind and compassionate towards yourself as you explore these themes. As you journey through Virgo season, it's a great time to reflect on your personal growth and self-improvement. By taking some time to journal about these topics, you can gain a deeper understanding of yourself and your goals. Here are some prompts to get you started: Setting Intentions for the New Moon Phase: What are your intentions for this new moon phase? What do you hope to achieve or work towards during this time? Focusing on Self-Improvement: What areas of your life are you focusing on for self-improvement? What specific actions are you taking to make progress in these areas? Overcoming Challenges and Obstacles: What challenges or obstacles have you faced in your journey towards self-improvement? How can you overcome these challenges and move forward? Utilizing Strengths for Personal Growth: What are your strengths and how can you utilize them to support your personal growth and self-improvement? Prioritizing Self-Care: How can you take care of yourself and prioritize your own needs during this new moon phase? What self-care practices can you incorporate into your routine? Seeking Support and Guidance: How can you seek out support and guidance from others as you work towards your goals for personal growth and self-improvement? Reflecting on Past Successes and Accomplishments: Reflect on your past successes and accomplishments related to self-improvement. How can you build on these achievements and continue to grow and evolve? Taking Small Steps for Daily Progress: What small steps can you take each day to work towards your goals for self-improvement? How can you make progress and stay motivated during this new moon phase? Celebrating Progress and Accomplishments: How can you celebrate your progress and accomplishments related to self-improvement during this new moon phase? What rewards or affirmations can you give yourself?
